definition_en: a large sports ground with seats around it, or the ancient Greek racecourse
core_image: 人群涌进环形的体育场看台
scene: 人群涌进体育场。 The crowd poured into the stadium.
sceneCN: 这里 stadium 是「体育场」（第 1 个义项）；句意：人群涌进体育场。

pos.zh: 斯塔德（古希腊长度单位）

senses.title: Sports ground
senses.definition: a large ground for sports with rows of seats around it
senses.definitionCN: 四周设有成排座位的巨大运动场地
senses.example: The crowd poured into the stadium.
senses.exampleCN: 人群涌进体育场。
senses.why: This is the everyday modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代最常见的义项。

senses.title: Greek racecourse
senses.definition: the ancient Greek track used for foot races
senses.definitionCN: 古希腊用于赛跑的跑道
senses.example: Runners raced in the ancient stadium.
senses.exampleCN: 赛跑者在古老的赛跑场上竞速。
senses.why: The word began as the name of this track.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初就是这条跑道的名称。

senses.title: Greek length unit
senses.definition: an ancient Greek unit of length, about one hundred and eighty-five metres
senses.definitionCN: 古希腊长度单位，约合一百八十五米
senses.example: The track was one stadium long.
senses.exampleCN: 这条跑道长一个斯塔德。
senses.why: The track length became a unit of measure.
senses.whyCN: 跑道的长度本身成了一种度量单位。

intro.en: Stadium comes from Greek stadion, a racecourse and a unit of length, through Latin stadium.
intro.cn: stadium 经拉丁语 stadium 来自希腊语 stadion，指赛跑场，也指长度单位。

items.en: Stadion meant a racecourse and its length.
items.cn: stadion 指赛跑场及其长度。

items.en: Stadium kept both the track and the measure.
items.cn: stadium 同时保留跑道与度量两义。

items.en: Stadium rarely named a place for races.
items.cn: 中古英语中 stadium 很少指赛跑场所。

items.en: The sports ground sense spread in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 体育场义项在十九世纪传播开来。

items.en: The Greek length sense survives in history books.
items.cn: 古希腊长度义仍见于史书。

note.en: Stadium is compared with look-alike words and words for sports grounds.
note.cn: 把 stadium 与形近词以及表示运动场地的词作比较。

a room for reading or work
a raised floor for performing
a central space for sports or shows
an area used for sports
a field for ball games

normalIntro.en: Stadium began as a Greek running track and now names the huge ground around it.
normalIntro.cn: stadium 原是希腊跑道，如今指环绕跑道的巨大体育场。

normal.en: The stadium was full.
normal.cn: 体育场坐满了人。

normal.en: They built a new stadium.
normal.cn: 他们建了一座新体育场。

normal.en: Flags waved around the stadium.
normal.cn: 旗帜在体育场四周飘扬。

normal.en: The Olympic stadium is huge.
normal.cn: 奥林匹克体育场非常巨大。

normal.en: Rain fell on the stadium roof.
normal.cn: 雨落在体育场顶棚上。

abstract.en: A track becomes a stage for thousands.
abstract.cn: 一条跑道，会变成千万人的舞台。

abstract.en: Seats turn watchers into one crowd.
abstract.cn: 座位把观看者聚成一片人海。

abstract.en: The measure of a race became a place.
abstract.cn: 赛跑的长度，最终成了场所之名。

examples.en: The crowd poured into the stadium.
examples.cn: 人群涌进体育场。

examples.en: Runners raced in the ancient stadium.
examples.cn: 赛跑者在古老的赛跑场上竞速。

examples.en: The track was one stadium long.
examples.cn: 这条跑道长一个斯塔德。

dict_mnemonic.text: stadium 是「体育场」，源自希腊语 stadion（赛跑场、长度单位）；复数是 stadiums，拉丁式复数为 stadia；football stadium 是足球场。

root: 经拉丁语 stadium 来自希腊语 stadion，指赛跑场及其长度；现代体育场环绕跑道而建，因而沿用此名。

sensesIntro.en: Stadium means a modern sports ground, the ancient Greek racecourse, or a Greek length unit.
sensesIntro.cn: stadium 指现代体育场、古希腊赛跑场，或古希腊长度单位。

core.en: A measured track where crowds watch races.
core.cn: 人群观看赛跑的有固定长度的跑道。

branches.en: Thousands fill the curved seats.
branches.cn: 成千上万人坐满弧形看台。

branches.en: Bare feet strike the ancient track.
branches.cn: 赤脚踩在古老的跑道上。

branches.en: A rope marks one length of the course.
branches.cn: 绳索标出跑道的一段长度。

branches.en: The modern ground keeps the old track.
branches.cn: 现代体育场仍保留了跑道。

branches.en: Both the ground and the measure grew from one word.
branches.cn: 场地与度量，都由同一个词生长出来。

intro.en: Stadium forms plurals and a few compounds.
intro.cn: stadium 构成复数和若干复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin form is stadium, from Greek stadion.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁语形式是 stadium，源自希腊语 stadion。

items.exampleCN: 聚集了体育场般庞大的人群。
这个大厅有阶梯式座位。

items.meaning: a concert tour of large grounds
items.example: The band began a stadium tour.
items.exampleCN: 乐队开始了体育场巡演。
体育场的人群欢呼起来。

definition_en: the time when day is ending and night is beginning, the dim light of that time, or a dark shadowy state
core_image: 山脊上的颜色一点点褪去，天边只剩一层薄薄的灰蓝
scene: 山脊上的颜色一点点褪去，鸟群开始向林中飞去。 The birds returned to the trees at dusk.
sceneCN: 这里 dusk 是「黄昏」（第 1 个义项：白昼将尽、夜晚初临的时刻）；句意是黄昏时鸟群飞回了林中。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「昏暗的；暮色的」
由 dusky 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「昏暗；暮色」
由本词加 -ish 构成，义为「略带暮色的；微暗的」

senses.title: The time when day ends
senses.definition: the time of day when the sun has set or is setting and night is beginning
senses.definitionCN: 太阳已落或正在落下、夜晚开始的时刻
senses.example: The birds returned to the trees at dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 黄昏时鸟群飞回了林中。
senses.why: Dusk began as an adjective for darkness; the noun then named the hour when that darkness first settles.
senses.whyCN: dusk 最初是表示「昏暗」的形容词，名词随后命名那片昏暗初次落下的时刻。

senses.title: The dim light of that hour
senses.definition: the soft, dim light seen in the sky just after sunset or just before night
senses.definitionCN: 日落后或入夜前天空中那种柔和而暗淡的光
senses.example: The dusk light made the road hard to see.
senses.exampleCN: 暮色让路很难看清。
senses.why: The hour and the light it contains are named together, so dusk can mean the glow as well as the time.
senses.whyCN: 那个时辰与它包含的光被一起命名，所以 dusk 既可指时刻，也可指那层光。

senses.title: A dark, shadowy state
senses.definition: a state of darkness or gloom, used mainly in literary writing
senses.definitionCN: 昏暗或阴郁的状态，主要用于书面文学
senses.example: The room lay in the dusk of drawn curtains.
senses.exampleCN: 房间笼罩在拉上窗帘后的幽暗里。
senses.why: Literature extends the evening image indoors: any half-dark place can be described as being in dusk.
senses.whyCN: 文学把黄昏的意象移到室内：任何半暗的地方都可以说处在 dusk 里。

intro.en: Dusk is an Old English word for dark or swarthy; the modern noun for twilight developed later from that adjective.
intro.cn: dusk 是古英语中表示「昏暗、黝黑」的词；现代表示「暮色」的名词义是后来从这个形容词发展出来的。

items.en: Old English dox or dusce described something dark, swarthy or shadowy, especially colour.
items.cn: 古英语 dox 或 dusce 形容昏暗、黝黑或阴影般的，尤其指颜色。

items.en: Middle English kept the adjective sense of dark and dim, applied to light and to surfaces.
items.cn: 中古英语保留了「昏暗、暗淡」的形容词义，用于光和表面。

items.en: The noun dusk for the twilight hour is recorded in the seventeenth century, growing from the adjective.
items.cn: 表示黄昏时刻的名词 dusk 在十七世纪有记录，是从形容词发展来的。

items.en: Literary writing extended dusk to any shadowy half-light, including indoor gloom.
items.cn: 文学写作把 dusk 扩展到任何幽暗的半光，包括室内的阴郁。

items.en: At dusk, dusk falls and from dusk till dawn fixed the word in everyday time expressions.
items.cn: at dusk、dusk falls 与 from dusk till dawn 把这个词固定在日常时间表达里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on dusk and one near-spelling word; the near-meaning group separates twilight, sunset and nightfall by exact time.
note.cn: 形近组收由 dusk 构成的词形和一个拼写相近的词；近义组按确切时段区分 twilight、sunset 与 nightfall。

entries.definition: Dark or dim, often with a soft or slightly sad tone; dusk plus -y.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「昏暗的、暮色的」，常带柔和或微带忧伤的语气，由 dusk 加 -y 构成。

entries.definition: The quality of being dark or dim; dusky plus -ness.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「昏暗、幽暗」，由 dusky 加 -ness 构成。

entries.definition: Slightly dark or dim; dusk plus the softening suffix -ish.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「微暗的、略带暮色的」，由 dusk 加弱化后缀 -ish 构成。

entries.definition: Fine dry particles of earth; it looks close to dusk but is a different noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「灰尘」，拼写与 dusk 接近，却是另一个名词。

entries.definition: The soft light between sunset and darkness, or between darkness and sunrise; wider than dusk.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「暮光、曙光」，指日落到黑暗之间或黑暗到日出之间的柔光，范围比 dusk 更宽。

entries.definition: The moment the sun disappears below the horizon; it marks the start of dusk.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「日落」，指太阳沉到地平线以下的时刻，是黄昏的开端。

entries.definition: The moment night begins; later and darker than dusk.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「入夜」，指夜晚开始的时刻，比黄昏更晚、更暗。

entries.definition: The later part of the day, from late afternoon to night; much broader than dusk.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「傍晚、晚上」，指一天的后半段，范围比 dusk 宽得多。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from the old adjective for dark and then narrow it to the hour when darkness first falls.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从表示「昏暗」的古老形容词出发，再收窄到黑暗最初落下的那个时辰。

normal.en: Dusk first meant dark as an adjective, then became the name of the darkening hour.
normal.cn: dusk 最初作形容词表示「昏暗」，后来变成那个渐渐变暗的时辰的名字。

normal.en: At dusk is the fixed phrase; dusk falls is the picture of the light giving way.
normal.cn: at dusk 是固定说法，dusk falls 是光线让位的画面。

normal.en: Dusk sits between sunset and nightfall: not yet night, no longer day.
normal.cn: dusk 位于日落与入夜之间：还不是夜，也不再是白天。

normal.en: Dusky is the adjective, duskiness the noun: the family keeps the dim light.
normal.cn: dusky 是形容词，duskiness 是名词，这一族都保留着那层昏暗的光。

normal.en: From dusk till dawn covers the whole night between two soft lights.
normal.cn: from dusk till dawn 覆盖两片柔光之间的整个夜晚。

abstract.en: Picture a hillside where colour drains away and only a grey-blue band remains.
abstract.cn: 想象一面山坡，颜色一点点褪去，只剩一条灰蓝的带子。

abstract.en: The same band appears indoors behind drawn curtains, as a room fills with half-light.
abstract.cn: 同一条带子又出现在拉上窗帘的室内，房间被半光填满。

abstract.en: Dusk is the seam between day and night, where neither one fully holds.
abstract.cn: dusk 是白昼与夜晚之间的接缝，两边都还未完全占住。

examples.en: The birds returned to the trees at dusk.
examples.cn: 黄昏时鸟群飞回了林中。

examples.en: By dusk the market had emptied.
examples.cn: 到黄昏时，市场已经空了。

examples.en: The dusk light made the road hard to see.
examples.cn: 暮色让路很难看清。

dict_mnemonic.text: dusk 是太阳落下后那层灰蓝的薄光：白天用尽，夜晚还没完全接手。

root: 古英语 dox 或 dusce 形容「昏暗、黝黑」，中古英语保留形容词义；十七世纪起名词 dusk 指黄昏时刻，十八至十九世纪文学又把它扩展到任何幽暗的半光。与 dust 拼写相近但来源不同。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of dusk move from the hour, to the light inside it, to any shadowy half-dark.
sensesIntro.cn: dusk 的三个义项从那个时辰，移到时辰里的光，再移到任何幽暗的半黑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hillside losing its colour as a thin grey-blue band remains.
core.cn: 核心意象：山坡褪去颜色，只剩一条薄薄的灰蓝。

branches.en: THE HOUR: the moment when day ends and night begins.
branches.cn: 时辰线：白昼结束、夜晚开始的时刻。

branches.en: THE LIGHT: the soft dim glow left in the sky at that hour.
branches.cn: 光线线：那个时辰天空里留下的柔和暗光。

branches.en: THE GLOOM: any shadowy half-dark, especially indoors in literature.
branches.cn: 幽暗线：任何阴影般的半黑，尤指文学中的室内。

branches.en: TIME AND GLOW: the word names both the hour and what fills it.
branches.cn: 时辰与光：这个词同时命名那个时刻和充满它的光。

branches.en: FROM SKY TO ROOM: the same dim light is carried indoors as gloom.
branches.cn: 从天空到室内：同一种暗光被带进屋里，成为幽暗。

intro.en: Dusk is a native English word; English adds -y, -ness and -ish, and fixed phrases carry most of its use.
intro.cn: dusk 是本族语英语词；英语加 -y、-ness、-ish，而它的用法多由固定短语承担。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source; Latin crepusculum, twilight, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 crepusculum（暮色）只是语义上的对应。

items.example: The word began as an adjective and became a noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个词从形容词开始，后来成为名词。
它出现在 dusk falls 中。

items.example: It appears in from dusk till dawn.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 from dusk till dawn 中。
它出现在 at dusk 中。
它出现在 by dusk 中。

由 dusky 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「昏暗；暮色」
由本词加 -ish 构成，义为「略带暮色的；微暗的」

definition_en: the set of letters used for writing a language, arranged in a fixed order
core_image: 墙上挂着一张从 A 排到 Z 的字母表
scene: 幼儿园的墙上贴着一张大大的字母表，孩子们每天跟着念。 The children sang the alphabet together before class.
sceneCN: 这里 alphabet 是「字母表」（第 1 个义项：一种语言全部字母的固定排列）；句意是上课前孩子们一起唱字母歌。

senses.title: The letters of a language
senses.titleCN: 字母表（全部字母的集合）
senses.definition: the complete set of letters that a written language uses
senses.definitionCN: 一种书面语言所使用的全部字母的总和
senses.example: The English alphabet has twenty-six letters.
senses.exampleCN: 英语字母表有二十六个字母。
senses.why: The word began as the names of the first two Greek letters, alpha and beta, and those two names came to stand for the whole set.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是希腊头两个字母 alpha 与 beta 的名字，后来这两个名字就代表整套字母。

senses.title: A fixed ordering
senses.definition: the conventional sequence of those letters, used for listing and looking things up
senses.definitionCN: 这些字母约定俗成的先后次序，用于排列条目与查找
senses.example: Names on the list are arranged by alphabet, not by age.
senses.exampleCN: 名单上的名字按字母顺序排列，而不是按年龄。
senses.why: Because the alphabet is learned as an ordered recitation, the word also names the order itself, which is how dictionaries and indexes work.
senses.whyCN: 因为字母表是作为有次序的背诵内容学会的，所以这个词也指这套次序本身，字典与索引正是靠它编排。

intro.en: Alphabet is a rare word whose history is visible in its first two sounds.
intro.cn: alphabet 是个少见的词，它的来历就写在开头两个音里。

items.en: Alpha was the name of the first letter, borrowed from a Phoenician letter meaning 'ox'.
items.cn: alpha 是第一个字母的名称，借自腓尼基字母，原意为「牛」。

items.en: Beta named the second letter and is the source of the English word beta.
items.cn: beta 是第二个字母的名称，也是英语 beta 的来源。

items.en: The Greeks joined the two names into alphabetos, a name for the whole set of letters.
items.cn: 希腊人把两个名字连成 alphabetos，用来指整套字母。

items.en: Latin took the Greek word as alphabetum, and the learned languages of Europe passed it on.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入为 alphabetum，欧洲的学术语言再把它传下去。

items.en: English alphabet appears in the sixteenth century and later yields alphabetical and alphabetize.
items.cn: 英语 alphabet 在十六世纪出现，后来派生出 alphabetical 与 alphabetize。

note.en: The look-alike group traces the Greek letter names; the near-meaning group contrasts writing systems.
note.cn: 形近组追溯希腊字母名；近义组对比不同的书写系统。

entries.definition: the first letter of the Greek alphabet
entries.definitionCN: 希腊字母表的第一个字母

entries.definition: the second letter of the Greek alphabet
entries.definitionCN: 希腊字母表的第二个字母

entries.definition: arranged in the order of the alphabet
any organised method of writing a language
entries.definitionCN: 书写一种语言的任何成套方法

entries.definition: the set of written characters used for a language
entries.definitionCN: 一种语言使用的整套书写符号

entries.definition: a writing system whose signs stand for syllables, not single letters
entries.definitionCN: 符号代表音节而非单个字母的书写系统

normalIntro.en: Alpha plus beta: the alphabet is named after its first two letters.
normalIntro.cn: alpha 加 beta：字母表正是用它头两个字母命名的。

normal.en: Say the first two Greek letters and you have said alphabet.
normal.cn: 念出希腊头两个字母，就说出了 alphabet。

normal.en: The English alphabet runs from A to Z.
normal.cn: 英语字母表从 A 排到 Z。

normal.en: Alphabetical adds -ical: arranged by letters.
normal.cn: alphabetical 加 -ical：按字母排列的。

normal.en: A dictionary is the alphabet put to work.
normal.cn: 字典就是让字母顺序干活。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AL-pha-bet.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：AL-pha-bet。

abstract.en: Picture a wall chart from A down to Z.
abstract.cn: 想象一张从 A 排到 Z 的挂图。

abstract.en: See a child singing the letters in order.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子按顺序唱字母。

abstract.en: Imagine a library shelf sorted by first letter.
abstract.cn: 想象按首字母排好的书架。

examples.en: Children usually learn the alphabet before they can read.
examples.cn: 孩子通常先学字母表，然后才学会阅读。

examples.en: The index lists all the places in alphabet order.
examples.cn: 索引按字母顺序列出所有地点。

examples.en: Some languages use an alphabet of more than forty letters.
examples.cn: 有些语言使用的字母表包含四十多个字母。

dict_mnemonic.text: alpha 与 beta 是希腊头两个字母，把它们连起来就得到「字母表」。

root: 希腊语 alphabetos 由头两个字母名 alpha 与 beta 连成，指整套字母；拉丁语作 alphabetum，十六世纪进入英语，并派生出 alphabetical、alphabetize 等词。

sensesIntro.en: From a name for the letter set comes a second use for its fixed order.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「整套字母」的名称，又生出「这套固定次序」的用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: A to Z hung on the classroom wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：从 A 到 Z 挂在教室墙上。

branches.en: the twenty-six letters of English
branches.cn: 英语的二十六个字母

branches.en: the Greek letters used in science
branches.cn: 科学中使用的希腊字母

branches.en: names sorted in a list
branches.cn: 名单按字母排序

branches.en: an index built on first letters

intro.en: The word is Greek in origin, and its family grows with Latin-style suffixes.
intro.cn: 这个词源自希腊语，它的词族靠拉丁式后缀扩展。

latinIntro.en: The Greek base alphabet- was passed through Latin, which supplies the combining forms below.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊词基 alphabet- 经拉丁语传来，下面列出相关的构词成分。

items.meaning: the act of sorting by letters

definition_en: an artist who paints pictures, or a worker who paints surfaces
core_image: 同一只手，一边在画布上安排颜色，一边在墙上把颜色铺平
scene: 装修现场，工人把梯子挪到墙边，准备刷第二遍。 The painter moved the ladder and began the second coat.
sceneCN: 这里 painter 指「以粉刷、涂漆为业的工人」（第 2 个义项：给建筑表面涂漆的油漆工）；句意为油漆工挪好梯子，开始刷第二遍；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: paint + -ing（动作或结果）→ 绘画；从「人」转到「活动与产物」
painter + -ly（形容词）→ 有笔触感的；从「人」转到「画面风格」
paint + work（成品）→ 漆面；从「动作」转到「表面结果」
paint + -ed（分词）→ 上过漆的；从「动作」转到「状态」

senses.title: An artist who paints pictures
senses.definition: a person who makes pictures with paint as an artist
senses.definitionCN: 以绘画为艺术创作的人
senses.example: The painter worked standing up, with the canvas on an easel.
senses.exampleCN: 这位画家站着作画，画布放在画架上。
senses.why: The agent suffix -er turns paint into 'one who paints'; in the art world that person is the maker of pictures.
senses.whyCN: 施事后缀 -er 把 paint 变成「涂绘的人」；在艺术界，这个人就是图画的制作者。

senses.title: A worker who paints surfaces
senses.definition: a tradesperson who applies paint to buildings and other surfaces
senses.definitionCN: 给建筑及其他表面涂漆的行业工人
senses.example: The painter moved the ladder and began the second coat.
senses.exampleCN: 油漆工挪好梯子，开始刷第二遍。
senses.why: The verb's everyday sense is 'coat a surface', so the same agent noun also names the trade that does it for pay.
senses.whyCN: 动词的日常义是「涂覆表面」，因此同一个施事名词也命名以此为报酬的行业。

senses.title: An artist known for a subject
senses.titleCN: 以某类题材著称的画家
senses.definition: an artist identified with a particular subject or genre
senses.definitionCN: 与某一题材或画类紧密相连的艺术家
senses.example: He was a painter of harbours before he was a painter of battles.
senses.exampleCN: 他先是画港口的画家，后来才画战役。
senses.why: The of-phrase narrows the artist's identity to what he habitually depicts, a common way of naming artistic specialism.
senses.whyCN: of 短语把艺术家的身份收窄到他惯常描绘之物，这是命名艺术专长的常见方式。

senses.title: An artist known for a medium
senses.titleCN: 以某种媒介著称的画家
senses.definition: an artist identified with a particular medium, as in oil painter
senses.definitionCN: 与某种媒介相连的艺术家，如油画家
senses.example: As an oil painter she distrusted quick sketches.
senses.exampleCN: 作为油画家，她不信任快速素描。
senses.why: Compounds put the medium before the agent, so the painter is defined by the material whose craft he has mastered.
senses.whyCN: 复合词把媒介放在施事者前，因此画家由他所精通的材料来界定。

senses.title: A painter in art history
senses.definition: a painter as a historical figure studied in art history
senses.definitionCN: 作为艺术史研究对象的历史人物
senses.example: The catalogue lists every painter represented in the collection.
senses.exampleCN: 图录列出了收藏中出现的每一位画家。
senses.why: The discipline turns individual makers into catalogue entries and attributions, so painter becomes a historical category.
senses.whyCN: 学科把个体创作者变成图录条目与归属判断，因此 painter 成为历史类别。

senses.title: An amateur or hobby painter
senses.definition: a person who paints for pleasure rather than professionally
senses.definitionCN: 为乐趣而非职业作画的人
senses.example: My uncle is a painter on Sundays and a clerk all week.
senses.exampleCN: 我叔叔周日是画家，其余时间是小职员。
senses.why: An agent noun does not require payment, so anyone who performs the action can be called a painter, including a hobbyist.
senses.whyCN: 施事名词不要求报酬，因此任何执行该动作的人都能被称为 painter，包括业余爱好者。

senses.title: A sign or lettering painter
senses.definition: a craftsman who paints signs, lettering or decorative surfaces
senses.definitionCN: 绘制招牌、字体或装饰表面的工匠
senses.example: The sign painter lettered the shop window by hand.
senses.exampleCN: 招牌画工用手工给橱窗写字。
senses.why: Compound specialisms preserve older workshop senses: the painter is the skilled hand in a named trade, not necessarily a fine artist.
senses.whyCN: 复合专名保留较早的工坊义：painter 是某个具名行当里的熟练手，不一定是纯艺术家。

senses.title: A workshop painter
senses.definition: a painter employed in a master's workshop to execute parts of works
senses.definitionCN: 受雇于名家工坊、执行作品局部的画师
senses.example: Many panels were finished by a workshop painter rather than the master.
senses.exampleCN: 许多木板画是由工坊画师而非名家本人完成的。
senses.why: Before the modern studio, paintings were made by teams; the word names each hand in the division of labour.
senses.whyCN: 在现代工作室出现之前，绘画由团队完成；这个词命名分工中的每一只手。

intro.en: Painter comes from Old French peintor, from Latin pictor, an agent noun from pingere 'to paint'; a separate homograph for a boat rope has a different origin. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: painter 来自古法语 peintor，上溯拉丁 pictor，即 pingere「绘画」的施事名词；另有一个指船缆的同形词，来源不同。年代均为约数。

items.en: Pingere meant 'to paint, depict, stain'; its deeper root is reconstructed as *peig- 'to cut, mark'.
items.cn: pingere 意为「绘画、描绘、染色」；其更早词根拟为 *peig-「切、刻痕」。

items.en: Pictor was the agent noun 'painter', formed from the stem of pingere; it named both the artist and the craftsman.
items.cn: pictor 是施事名词「画家」，由 pingere 的词干构成；既指艺术家，也指工匠。

items.en: Old French peintor carried the word into English; the same French form also named a rope on a boat, a confusing coincidence of spelling.
items.cn: 古法语 peintor 把这个词带入英语；同一法语形式还指船上的一条缆绳，这是令人困惑的拼写巧合。

items.en: English painter is recorded in the early fourteenth century as 'artist who paints pictures'.
items.cn: 英语 painter 于 14 世纪初有记录，指「作画的艺术家」。

items.en: By about 1400 the word also meant 'workman who colours surfaces with paint'.
items.cn: 到约 1400 年，这个词也指「用颜料给表面着色的工人」。

items.en: The rope painter of the mid-fourteenth century probably comes from a different Old French word and ultimately from Latin pendere 'to hang'; that path is uncertain, and the two words are unrelated despite identical spelling.
items.cn: 14 世纪中叶指缆绳的 painter 可能来自另一个古法语词，最终上溯拉丁 pendere「悬挂」；这条路径不确定，两个词尽管拼写相同却并不同源。

note.en: Group one holds the same-stem words and the unrelated rope homograph; group two holds occupations and art roles that overlap but stress a different material or setting.
note.cn: 第一组是同词干词以及无关的缆绳同形词；第二组是重叠但强调不同材料或场景的职业与艺术角色。

entries.definition: A rope used to tie a boat; it is a homograph, not a sense of the artist word, and comes probably from Latin pendere 'to hang'.
entries.definitionCN: 系船的缆绳；是同形异源词，不是艺术家一词的义项，可能来自拉丁 pendere「悬挂」。

entries.definition: A picture or the activity of painting; painter is the person who performs it.
entries.definitionCN: 画作或绘画活动；painter 是执行它的人。

entries.definition: To coat or depict, or the coloured substance; painter is the agent.
entries.definitionCN: 涂覆或描绘，或彩色材料；painter 是施事者。

entries.definition: Having visible brushwork or a soft, painted quality; it describes a surface, not a person.
entries.definitionCN: 有可见笔触或柔和绘画感的；描述表面，而非人。

entries.definition: A maker of art in any medium; painter is the narrower word for one who works in paint.
entries.definitionCN: 任何媒介的艺术创作者；painter 是专指用颜料者的较窄词。

entries.definition: A worker who paints and papers interiors; painter stresses the paintwork, decorator the whole finish.
entries.definitionCN: 给室内刷漆贴墙纸的工人；painter 强调涂漆，decorator 强调整体饰面。

entries.definition: A painter who works on walls; painter is neutral about scale or support.
entries.definitionCN: 在墙上作画的画家；painter 对尺幅与支撑物不加限定。

entries.definition: A painter or photographer specialising in portraits; painter names no subject.
entries.definitionCN: 专攻肖像的画家或摄影师；painter 不限定题材。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: paint + -er 'one who': the person who paints, whether canvas or wall.
normal.cn: paint + -er「从事者」：涂绘的人，无论画布还是墙面。

normal.en: Latin pictor is the ancestor, and picture and pigment share the stem.
normal.cn: 祖先是拉丁 pictor，picture 与 pigment 共享同一词干。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: portrait painter, house painter, sign painter.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分义项：肖像画家、房屋油漆工、招牌画工。

normal.en: The family runs paint, painter, painting, painted and painterly.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 paint、painter、painting、painted 与 painterly。

normal.en: The rope painter is a different word: same spelling, different origin, no family relation.
normal.cn: 指缆绳的 painter 是另一个词：拼写相同、来源不同、没有亲缘关系。

abstract.en: Picture one hand that can both compose a face and flatten a wall.
abstract.cn: 想象同一只手既能安排一张脸，也能把一面墙铺平。

abstract.en: Picture a ladder standing where an easel might also stand.
abstract.cn: 想象一架梯子立在本可放画架的地方。

abstract.en: Picture a name that two unrelated things have learned to share.
abstract.cn: 想象一个被两件无关之物共用的名字。

examples.en: The painter left the canvas unfinished when the light changed.
examples.cn: 光线一变，画家就停下未完成的画。

examples.en: A painter and decorator was repainting the stairwell.
examples.cn: 一位油漆装饰工正在重刷楼梯间。

examples.en: The workshop painter filled in the background while the master worked on the face.
examples.cn: 名家画脸时，工坊画师补画背景。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「paint（涂颜料）+ -er（人）」——涂颜料的人 → 画家／油漆工

root: 拉丁 pingere「绘画、染色」的施事名词 pictor，经古法语 peintor 进入英语，14 世纪初指画家，约 1400 年兼指油漆工。指船缆的 painter 为同形异源词，来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses distinguish the fine artist from the trade worker, then split by subject, medium, historical role, amateur status, sign work and workshop division of labour.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把纯艺术家与行业工人分开，再按题材、媒介、历史角色、业余身份、招牌工作与工坊分工细分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand arranges colour on a canvas and flattens colour on a wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一只手在画布上安排颜色，也在墙上把颜色铺平。

branches.en: THE PICTURE MAKER: the artist whose product is an image.
branches.cn: 作画者：产物是一幅图像的艺术家。

branches.en: THE SURFACE COATER: the same agent noun in the building trade.
branches.cn: 表面涂覆者：同一施事名词在建筑行业中的用法。

branches.en: SUBJECT: identity narrowed to what is depicted.
branches.cn: 题材：身份被收窄到所描绘之物。

branches.en: MEDIUM AND HISTORY: the material mastered, then the figure in the catalogue.
branches.cn: 媒介与历史：所精通的材料，然后是图录中的人物。

branches.en: ROLES AROUND THE CRAFT: amateur, sign worker and workshop hand.
branches.cn: 手艺周边的角色：业余者、招牌工与工坊画师。

intro.en: Painter is a verb stem plus the agent suffix -er; the stem's Latin ancestor builds a whole family of images, materials and actions.
intro.cn: painter 是动词词干加施事后缀 -er；其词干的拉丁祖先构成一整族图像、材料与动作词。

latinIntro.en: Latin pictor is the direct model; pingere also yields picture, pigment, depict and pictorial.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 pictor 是直接模板；pingere 还给出 picture、pigment、depict 与 pictorial。

The sky is handled in a painterly way.
items.exampleCN: 天空以绘画式手法处理。

items.exampleCN: 壁带描绘一支游行队伍。

The picture is older than the frame.

definition_zh: 现代化；使社会、经济、制度或设备变得现代的过程；现代化理论；技术更新
definition_en: the process of making a society, economy, institution or equipment modern
core_image: 老厂房里，工人把最后一台手摇车床推出去，换上带屏幕的新机器
scene: 老厂房里，工人把最后一台手摇车床推出去，换上带屏幕的新机器， The factory's modernization replaced hand tools with computer-controlled machines.
sceneCN: 这里 modernization 指「设备与生产的技术更新」（第 3 个义项：技术层面的现代化）；句意为这家工厂的现代化用电脑控制的机器取代了手工工具。图中可辨识物件：手摇车床、带屏幕的新机器、搬运轨道、工人的手套；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 现代化；现代化的过程；技术更新

senses.title: The process of becoming modern
senses.definition: the broad process by which a society acquires modern industry, institutions and ways of life
senses.definitionCN: 一个社会获得现代工业、制度与生活方式的总过程
senses.example: Modernization changed the valley within one generation.
senses.exampleCN: 现代化在一代人的时间里改变了这座山谷。
senses.why: The suffix names a process rather than a state: the word looks at the movement toward modernity, not at modernity itself.
senses.whyCN: 后缀命名的是过程而不是状态：这个词看的是走向现代性的运动，而非现代性本身。

senses.title: The sociological paradigm
senses.definition: the body of theory that explains development as a series of stages from traditional to modern society
senses.definitionCN: 把发展解释为从传统社会到现代社会一系列阶段的理论总体
senses.example: Modernization was the dominant framework in development studies after the war.
senses.exampleCN: 战后，现代化曾是发展研究中的主导框架。
senses.why: A process this large needs a theory, so the same noun names the academic paradigm that tried to describe it.
senses.whyCN: 如此庞大的过程需要理论，因此同一个名词也命名试图描述它的学术范式。

senses.title: Technical upgrading of equipment
senses.definition: the replacement of old machinery, systems or methods with newer and more efficient ones
senses.definitionCN: 用更新、更高效的机器、系统或方法替换旧的
senses.example: The factory's modernization replaced hand tools with computer-controlled machines.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂的现代化用电脑控制的机器取代了手工工具。
senses.why: The grand process has a workshop-sized version: one machine at a time, the old is pushed out and the new is wired in.
senses.whyCN: 宏大的过程有一个车间大小的版本：一次换一台机器，旧的被推出去，新的被接上电线。

senses.title: Urban and infrastructural development
senses.definition: the building of roads, housing, water and power systems to modern standards
senses.definitionCN: 按现代标准建设道路、住房、供水与电力系统
senses.example: Modernization brought the first paved road to the fishing village.
senses.exampleCN: 现代化把第一条铺装路带到了这个渔村。
senses.why: Modern life has a physical shell, and the noun often names the laying of that shell: pipes, wires, asphalt.
senses.whyCN: 现代生活有一层物质外壳，这个名词常指铺这层外壳：管道、电线、沥青。

senses.title: Economic and industrial development
senses.definition: the shift from farming and small craft to industry, wage labour and higher output
senses.definitionCN: 从农业与手工副业转向工业、雇佣劳动与更高产量
senses.example: Economic modernization moved workers from the fields to the mills.
senses.exampleCN: 经济现代化把工人从田里移到了工厂。
senses.why: Economists use the word for the measurable part of the change: where people work and what they produce.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家用这个词指变化中可测量的部分：人在哪里工作、生产什么。

senses.title: Institutional and legal reform
senses.definition: the reform of government, law and administration along modern lines
senses.definitionCN: 按现代方式改革政府、法律与行政
senses.example: Legal modernization removed the old courts and created a written code.
senses.exampleCN: 法律现代化废除了旧法庭，制定了一部成文法典。
senses.why: Industry needs contracts and records, so the process reaches into courts, registries and tax offices.
senses.whyCN: 工业需要合同与记录，因此这一过程延伸到法院、登记处与税务所。

senses.title: Cultural change toward modern values
senses.definition: the spread of values such as mobility, individual choice, science and secular time
senses.definitionCN: 流动性、个人选择、科学与世俗时间观等价值的传播
senses.example: Modernization altered how families arranged marriages and kept time.
senses.exampleCN: 现代化改变了家庭安排婚姻与计算时间的方式。
senses.why: The process is not only machines: it changes what people expect from life and from each other.
senses.whyCN: 这个过程不只是机器：它改变人们对生活、对彼此的期待。

senses.title: The state of being modernized
senses.definition: the result of the process, viewed as a completed condition
senses.definitionCN: 过程的结果，被视为已完成的状态
senses.example: The port's modernization is visible in its cranes and its silence.
senses.exampleCN: 这座港口的现代化在吊车与寂静中都看得见。
senses.why: A process noun can be read backwards as a result: what has been modernized is now a condition.
senses.whyCN: 过程名词也可以倒过来读成结果：已经被现代化的东西，如今成了一种状态。

intro.en: Modernization is modern plus the verb ending -ize and the process ending -ation, ultimately from Late Latin modernus and modo. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: modernization 由 modern 加动词词尾 -ize 与过程词尾 -ation 构成，最终来自晚期拉丁语 modernus 与 modo。年代均为约数。

items.en: Modo meant just now. It is usually derived from modus, measure or manner, though that link is a standard account rather than a recorded certainty.
items.cn: modo 意为「刚刚」。通行说法认为它来自 modus「尺度、方式」，但这一联系只是标准解释，并非有记录的确证。

items.en: Late Latin modernus, of the present time, was built from the time word plus -nus.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 modernus 意为「当下的」，由这个时间词加 -nus 构成。

items.en: The verb ending -ize came through Latin -izare from Greek -izein, meaning to make, practise or become.
items.cn: 动词词尾 -ize 经拉丁语 -izare 来自希腊语 -izein，意为「使、从事或成为」。

items.en: The noun ending -ation came from Latin -atio, which named an action or its result.
items.cn: 名词词尾 -ation 来自拉丁语 -atio，表示动作或其结果。

items.en: Modernization appeared in the nineteenth century as industry and administration began to be described as a single process.
items.cn: modernization 在十九世纪出现，当时工业与行政开始被描述为同一个过程。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first English use of modernization is not securely dated, and the pre-Latin origin of modo and modus is unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定：modernization 在英语中的最早使用没有确切年代；modo 与 modus 在拉丁语之前的来源亦无定论。

note.en: The first group holds members of the same modern- family; the second holds processes that are often mistaken for modernization itself.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 modern- 词族的成员；第二组是常被误当作现代化本身的过程。

entries.definition: To make something modern; modernization is the process noun built from that verb.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物现代化；modernization 是由该动词构成的过程名词。

entries.definition: Belonging to the present age; it describes a thing, while modernization describes the change that made it so.
entries.definitionCN: 属于当下时代的；它描述事物，而 modernization 描述使之如此的变化。

entries.definition: The state of being modern; modernization is the road, modernity is the place arrived at.
entries.definitionCN: 现代的状态；modernization 是道路，modernity 是抵达的地方。

entries.definition: The artistic and intellectual movement that broke with inherited forms; it is cultural, while modernization is social and technical.
entries.definitionCN: 打破继承形式的艺术与思想运动；它属于文化，而 modernization 属于社会与技术。

entries.definition: Improvement in economic and social conditions; modernization is one model of how development should happen.
entries.definitionCN: 经济与社会状况的改善；现代化是关于发展应如何发生的一种模型。

entries.definition: The growth of manufacturing industry; it is one part of modernization, not the whole process.
entries.definitionCN: 制造业的增长；它是现代化的一部分，而非全过程。

entries.definition: Adoption of Western institutions and culture; critics use it to say that modernization was never neutral.
entries.definitionCN: 采纳西方的制度与文化；批评者用它指出现代化从来不是中立的。

entries.definition: An improvement to one machine or system; modernization suggests a broader and longer process.
entries.definitionCN: 对单台机器或系统的改进；modernization 暗示更广、更长的过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real modern stem, the real process endings and the phrases the word actually keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的 modern 词干、真实的过程词尾，以及这个词实际常用的搭配。

normal.en: modern plus the make-verb ending and the process ending: the word is literally the making of the modern.
normal.cn: modern 加表示「使……」的动词词尾与表示过程的名词词尾：这个词字面上就是「使现代的过程」。

normal.en: The family runs modern, modernize, modernization, modernity, modernism and modernizer.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 modern（现代的）、modernize（使现代化）、modernization（现代化）、modernity（现代性）、modernism（现代主义）、modernizer（推动现代化的人）。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: economic modernization, industrial modernization, technical modernization.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：经济现代化、工业现代化、技术现代化。

normal.en: The word is a road, not a destination: modernity is where the road arrives.
normal.cn: 这个词是一条路，不是终点：modernity 才是路抵达的地方。

normal.en: Its common critique is that it treats one model of development as universal.
normal.cn: 对它的常见批评是：它把一种发展模型当作普遍标准。

abstract.en: Picture an old lathe rolled out of a factory while a new machine is wired in.
abstract.cn: 想象一台旧车床被推出厂房，同时一台新机器正在接线。

abstract.en: Picture a village where the first paved road arrives before the first streetlight.
abstract.cn: 想象一个村庄，第一条铺装路先于第一盏路灯到来。

abstract.en: Picture a clock changing from church bells to factory whistles.
abstract.cn: 想象计时方式从教堂钟声变成工厂汽笛。

examples.en: Modernization promised wealth and delivered a new kind of dependence.
examples.cn: 现代化许诺财富，却交出一种新的依赖。

examples.en: The archive's modernization put every ledger online.
examples.cn: 档案馆的现代化把每一本账册都搬上了网。

examples.en: Social modernization changed the wedding more than the factory.
examples.cn: 社会现代化对婚礼的改变，胜过对工厂的改变。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摩登」加「化」——把旧东西一步步变成摩登的样子，就是现代化。

root: 由 modern 加动词词尾 -ize 与过程词尾 -ation 构成。modern 来自晚期拉丁语 modernus「当下的」，通行说法追溯至 modo「刚刚」，modo 又常被解释为来自 modus「尺度、方式」；-ize 经拉丁语 -izare 源自希腊语 -izein，-ation 来自拉丁语 -atio。modo 与 modus 的更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one process: a society, a theory, a machine, a road, an economy, a court, a value and finally the finished state.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个过程展开：一个社会、一套理论、一台机器、一条路、一个经济、一座法院、一种价值，最后是完成后的状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old machine rolled out while a new one is wired in.
core.cn: 核心意象：旧机器被推出，新机器正在接线。

branches.en: PROCESS AND RESULT: the same word can look forward to the change or backward at what has been changed.
branches.cn: 过程与结果：同一个词既可以向前看变化，也可以回头看在变化之后的状态。

branches.en: THEORY: the process becomes a paradigm that claims to explain all societies.
branches.cn: 理论：这个过程变成一套声称能解释所有社会的范式。

branches.en: MACHINE: the workshop-sized version, one lathe at a time.
branches.cn: 机器：车间大小的版本，一次换一台车床。

branches.en: ROAD AND ECONOMY: pipes, asphalt and wages make the new life possible.
branches.cn: 道路与经济：管道、沥青与工资使新生活成为可能。

branches.en: LAW AND VALUES: courts need written codes, and families need new expectations.
branches.cn: 法律与价值：法院需要成文法典，家庭需要新的期待。

intro.en: Modernization stacks a time adjective, a make-verb ending and a process noun ending.
intro.cn: modernization 叠了一个时间形容词、一个表示「使……」的动词词尾与一个过程名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin modo and modernus supply the adjective, Greek -izein through Latin supplies the verb, and Latin -atio supplies the process noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 modo 与 modernus 提供形容词，希腊语 -izein 经拉丁语提供动词，拉丁语 -atio 提供过程名词。

items.example: The adverb is usually linked to modus, measure.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词通常被联系到 modus「尺度」。

items.example: The adjective entered English through French.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词经法语进入英语。

items.example: The ending builds modernize and industrialize.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成 modernize（使现代化）与 industrialize（使工业化）。

items.example: The ending builds modernization and industrialization.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成 modernization（现代化）与 industrialization（工业化）。
现代化改变了这座港口。

items.example: The modernizer rebuilt the telegraph line.
items.exampleCN: 这位现代化推动者重建了电报线。

items.example: Modernity arrived before modernization was complete.
items.exampleCN: 现代性在现代化完成之前就到来了。

items.meaning: the cultural movement of the new
items.example: Modernism changed the gallery, not the factory.
items.exampleCN: 现代主义改变的是画廊，不是工厂。

definition_en: to condemn someone, to swear at something, or a word showing strong feeling
core_image: 一脚踩进泥坑，低声吐出一句骂
scene: 他一脚踩进泥坑，低声骂了一句。 He damned the driver who splashed him.
sceneCN: 这里 damned 是 damn 的过去式，指「咒骂」（第 1 个义项：用狠话骂人）；句意是他咒骂那个溅了他一身水的司机。

pos.zh: 丝毫；一点点（多用于否定）

senses.title: To condemn or swear at
senses.definition: to condemn someone or swear at something in anger
senses.definitionCN: 愤怒地谴责某人或咒骂某事
senses.example: He damned the driver who splashed him.
senses.exampleCN: 他咒骂那个溅了他一身水的司机。
senses.why: The word began as a judgement and ended as a shout.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从审判开始，最后变成一声喊。

senses.title: An angry exclamation
senses.definition: a short angry word used when something goes wrong
senses.definitionCN: 事情出错时脱口而出的短促气话
senses.example: Damn, I left the keys inside.
senses.exampleCN: 该死，我把钥匙落在里面了。
senses.why: When a plan breaks, the mouth reaches for the strongest word it has.
senses.whyCN: 计划一碎，嘴就去抓它最有力的那个词。

senses.title: Not a bit
senses.definition: a very small amount, used in negative statements
senses.definitionCN: 极少的量，多用于否定句
senses.example: He does not care a damn.
senses.exampleCN: 他一点也不在乎。
senses.why: The least valuable thing you can name becomes the measure of nothing.
senses.whyCN: 能说出的最不值钱的东西，就成了「零」的度量。

intro.en: Damn comes from Latin damnare, to condemn, from damnum, loss, through Old French damner.
intro.cn: damn 源自拉丁语 damnare（宣判有罪），其根为 damnum（损失），经古法语 damner 进入英语。

items.en: Damnum meant loss or harm.
items.cn: damnum 意为损失或伤害。

items.en: Damnare meant to condemn to loss or punishment.
items.cn: damnare 意为判处损失或刑罚。

items.en: Damner carried the sense of condemning a soul.
items.cn: damner 带有判灵魂有罪的意思。

items.en: Damn entered English for eternal punishment.
items.cn: damn 进入英语，指永罚。

items.en: It softened into a common swear word and an intensifier.
items.cn: 它软化成常见的骂人话和加强语气的词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dam- sound, and the meaning group names other ways of condemning.
note.cn: 形近组共享 dam- 的读音，近义组列出其他谴责的说法。

entries.definition: a wall that holds back water
slightly wet
an old title for a woman
to wish harm on someone in words
to say strongly that something is wrong
to use rude words in anger

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a foot in the mud and end with a care that amounts to nothing.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一脚踩进泥里开始，落到一份少到等于没有的在乎。

normal.en: Damn began in court and ended in the street.
normal.cn: damn 从法庭出发，最后落在了街上。

normal.en: A slipped foot is enough to make the word appear.
normal.cn: 脚下一滑，就够让这个词冒出来。

normal.en: The strongest word loses strength each time it is used.
normal.cn: 最狠的词，每用一次就弱一分。

normal.en: Not caring a damn is caring the smallest possible amount.
normal.cn: 一点也不在乎，就是只在乎那么一丁点。

normal.en: When words fail, damn is what the mouth finds.
normal.cn: 话不够用时，嘴就找到了 damn。

abstract.en: Picture a clean shoe sinking into dark mud.
abstract.cn: 想象一只干净的鞋陷进黑泥里。

abstract.en: Picture a hand slapping a table once, hard.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手重重拍了一下桌子。

abstract.en: Picture a scale with nothing at all on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一台秤上什么也没放。

examples.en: He damned the driver who splashed him.
examples.cn: 他咒骂那个溅了他一身水的司机。

examples.en: Damn, I left the keys inside.
examples.cn: 该死，我把钥匙落在里面了。

examples.en: He does not care a damn.
examples.cn: 他一点也不在乎。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 damn 记成「判」：原本是宣判有罪，后来变成一句脱口而出的骂。

root: 源自拉丁语 damnare（宣判有罪），出自 damnum（损失），经古法语 damner 进入英语；本义是判定某人该受惩罚，后弱化为咒骂与表示恼怒的感叹词。

sensesIntro.en: From a solemn judgement, to a street-corner swear, to a measure of utter indifference.
sensesIntro.cn: 从庄重的判决，到街角的骂声，再到衡量彻底不在乎的量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand striking a table after something goes wrong.
core.cn: 核心意象：事情出错后，一只手重重拍在桌上。

branches.en: The oldest sense is a judgement that condemns.
branches.cn: 最古老的意思，是宣判有罪的裁断。

branches.en: The same word becomes a short cry when things break.
branches.cn: 事情崩了时，同一个词变成一声短喊。

branches.en: In the negative it measures how little one cares.
branches.cn: 在否定句里，它衡量一个人有多不在乎。

branches.en: A curse and a cry of anger come from one root.
branches.cn: 诅咒和怒喊，出自同一个根。

branches.en: A word of anger can also measure nothing at all.
branches.cn: 一句怒气话，也能用来衡量「什么都没有」。

intro.en: Damn belongs to the Latin damnum family, where loss grows into judgement and into swearing.
intro.cn: damn 属于拉丁语 damnum 这一族，「损失」在这里长成审判与骂声。

latinIntro.en: The Latin damnare, to condemn, is the root under damn and damnation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 damnare（宣判有罪）是 damn 与 damnation 的根。

items.example: They damned the plan as foolish.
items.exampleCN: 他们谴责这个计划愚蠢。
那该死的噪音一刻不停。

items.example: The old tale warned of damnation.
items.exampleCN: 那个古老的故事警告人会有永罚。

items.example: Damn it, the bus has gone.
She does not give a damn about it.
items.exampleCN: 她一点也不在乎这件事。

items.example: The damage was easy to see.

definition_en: the physical parts of a computer, or tools and metal goods for the home
core_image: 货架上摆满锤子、钉子和一把把螺丝刀
scene: 电脑硬件需要定期升级。 The computer hardware needs an upgrade.
sceneCN: 这里 hardware 是「硬件」（第 1 个义项）；句意：电脑硬件需要定期升级。

senses.title: Computer machinery
senses.definition: the physical parts of a computer rather than its programs
senses.definitionCN: 计算机的实体部件，而非其程序
senses.example: The computer hardware needs an upgrade.
senses.exampleCN: 电脑硬件需要升级。
senses.why: This is the modern technical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代技术义项。

senses.title: Metal goods for the home
senses.definition: tools and metal items sold for building and repair
senses.definitionCN: 建筑与修理用的工具和金属制品
senses.example: He bought nails at the hardware store.
senses.exampleCN: 他在五金店买了钉子。
senses.why: This is the original shop sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最早的五金店义项。

senses.title: Heavy equipment
senses.definition: large machines or weapons used by an army
senses.definitionCN: 军队使用的大型机械或武器
senses.example: The army moved its hardware north.
senses.exampleCN: 军队把装备向北调动。
senses.why: Things made of hard metal became tools of force.
senses.whyCN: 硬金属制品，成了武力的工具。

intro.en: Hardware is hard plus ware, goods, first naming metal goods and later computer parts.
intro.cn: hardware 是 hard 加 ware（货物），先指金属制品，后指计算机部件。

items.en: Waru meant goods or articles.
items.cn: waru 意为货物、物品。

items.en: Hardware named goods made of hard metal.
items.cn: hardware 指硬金属制成的货物。

items.en: A hardware store sold tools and nails.
items.cn: 五金店卖工具与钉子。

items.en: The word named military equipment.
items.cn: 这个词指军事装备。

items.en: Computers gave it a new sense.
items.cn: 计算机赋予了它新义。

note.en: Hardware is compared with look-alike words and with words for equipment.
note.cn: 把 hardware 与形近词以及表示设备的词作比较。

hats and caps
a hard life
the things needed for an activity
a thing used to do work
machines as a group

normalIntro.en: Hardware began as hammers and nails and now also means the metal inside a computer.
normalIntro.cn: hardware 起初是锤子和钉子，如今也指电脑里的金属部件。

normal.en: The hardware store is on the corner.
normal.cn: 五金店在街角。

normal.en: He fixed the shelf with new hardware.
normal.cn: 他用新五金件修好了架子。

normal.en: This laptop has strong hardware.
normal.cn: 这台笔记本电脑硬件很强。

normal.en: Hardware and software must work together.
normal.cn: 硬件与软件必须协同工作。

normal.en: The truck carried military hardware.
normal.cn: 卡车运载着军事装备。

abstract.en: What is hard in the hand is easy to name.
abstract.cn: 手里坚硬的东西，最容易命名。

abstract.en: A body of metal still needs a mind of code.
abstract.cn: 金属的身躯，仍需代码的心。

abstract.en: Tools change, but the hand that holds them is old.
abstract.cn: 工具会变，握工具的手却很古老。

examples.en: The computer hardware needs an upgrade.
examples.cn: 电脑硬件需要升级。

examples.en: He bought nails at the hardware store.
examples.cn: 他在五金店买了钉子。

examples.en: The army moved its hardware north.
examples.cn: 军队把装备向北调动。

dict_mnemonic.text: hardware 是 hard 加 ware（制品），原指金属五金，所以五金店叫 hardware store；计算机时代又指看得见摸得着的「硬件」，与 software 相对。

root: hard（硬的）加 ware（制品、货物）；原指硬金属制成的五金器具，后扩展为军事装备与计算机硬件。

sensesIntro.en: Hardware is the metal inside a computer, the tools sold in a shop, or heavy military equipment.
sensesIntro.cn: hardware 是电脑中的实体部件、商店里卖的五金工具，或军队的重型装备。

core.en: Something hard that can be held.
core.cn: 能握在手里的硬东西。

branches.en: A case opens to show boards and chips.
branches.cn: 机箱打开，露出主板与芯片。

branches.en: Drawers hold screws and hinges.
branches.cn: 抽屉里装着螺丝与铰链。

branches.en: Trucks carry steel to a distant camp.
branches.cn: 卡车把钢铁运往远方营地。

branches.en: Both a computer and an army rely on solid metal.
branches.cn: 电脑与军队，都依赖坚实的金属。

branches.en: The shop and the machine share one material.
branches.cn: 店铺与机器，共用同一种材料。

intro.en: Hardware is a compound of hard and ware and has no plural.
intro.cn: hardware 是 hard 与 ware 的复合词，没有复数形式。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.

items.example: The hardware upgrade doubled the speed.

definition_en: to wait for something, or to be waiting for someone
core_image: 一个人站在站台上，眼睛望着铁轨尽头
scene: 站台上只有一个人，风把外套吹起。 A small crowd awaited the last train.
sceneCN: 这里 await 是「等待」（第 1 个义项：等候某人或某事到来）；句意是一小群人在等末班车。

pos.zh: 动词：等待；期待；将降临于

derivatives.zh: 基础词，义为「等待」，await 由 a- 加 wait 构成
由 wait 加 -ing 构成，义为「等待」
由 wait 加 -er 构成，义为「服务员」

senses.title: Wait for
senses.definition: to wait for someone or something to arrive
senses.definitionCN: 等候某人或某物到来
senses.example: A small crowd awaited the last train.
senses.exampleCN: 一小群人在等末班车。
senses.why: Await is the old verb wait with the prefix a-, and it kept the transitive use; what you await is the object of your waiting.
senses.whyCN: await 是古动词 wait 加前缀 a- 的形式，保留了及物用法；你 await 的东西就是等待的对象。

senses.title: Be in store for someone
senses.definition: to be going to happen to someone, especially something important
senses.definitionCN: 即将发生在某人身上，尤指重要的事
senses.example: A warm welcome awaited the visitors.
senses.exampleCN: 热烈的欢迎在等着来访者。
senses.why: If an event is waiting for a person, the person will meet it soon, so await can mean what is in store for someone.
senses.whyCN: 如果一件事在等着某人，那个人很快就会遇上它，所以 await 也能表示某事在等着某人。

intro.en: Await is wait with an old prefix that adds direction.
intro.cn: await 是 wait 加上一个表示方向的老前缀。

items.en: waitier meant 'to watch'.
items.cn: waitier 意为「守望」。

items.en: wait meant 'a watch or guard'.
items.cn: wait 意为「看守、守卫」。

items.en: awaiten meant 'to watch for'.
items.cn: awaiten 意为「守望等待」。

items.en: await took on the sense of expecting.
items.cn: await 获得「期待」之义。

items.en: It survives mainly in formal writing.
items.cn: 如今主要用于正式文体。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the a- opening; the near-meaning group gives verbs of waiting and expecting.
note.cn: 形近组都以 a- 开头；近义组是表示等待与期待的动词。

entries.definition: to give a prize officially
not asleep
knowing that something exists
to stay until something happens
to think something will happen
to look forward to something

normalIntro.en: Await is a formal wait that takes its object directly.
normalIntro.cn: await 是正式的 wait，后面直接带宾语。

normal.en: Await a thing, but wait for a thing.
normal.cn: await 直接带宾语，wait 要加 for。

normal.en: Await is common in letters and news: we await your reply.
normal.cn: await 常见于书信与新闻。

normal.en: The stress is on the second syllable: a-WAIT.
normal.cn: 重音在第二音节。

normal.en: The past tense is awaited, not await.
normal.cn: 过去式是 awaited。

normal.en: Long awaited is a common phrase before a noun.
normal.cn: long awaited 常放在名词前。

abstract.en: See one figure on a platform staring down the rails.
abstract.cn: 想象站台上一个人望着铁轨尽头。

abstract.en: See a door about to open for a guest.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门即将为客人打开。

abstract.en: See a letter held in both hands, unopened.
abstract.cn: 想象双手捧着一封未拆的信。

examples.en: A small crowd awaited the last train.
examples.cn: 一小群人在等末班车。

examples.en: A warm welcome awaited the visitors.
examples.cn: 热烈的欢迎在等着来访者。

examples.en: We await your reply with interest.
examples.cn: 我们期待您的回复。

dict_mnemonic.text: a-（向）加 wait（守望）：把目光一直投向远处，等那个人或那件事出现。

root: 由 a- 加 wait 构成；wait 源自古法语 waitier「守望」，经盎格鲁-诺曼语 wait「看守」进入英语；await 保留了及物用法，多用于正式文体。

sensesIntro.en: Waiting for an arrival and waiting for a coming event are the same posture of attention.
sensesIntro.cn: 等一个人到来与等一件事降临，是同一种张望的姿态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gaze fixed on the far end of the rails.
core.cn: 核心意象：目光固定在铁轨尽头。

branches.en: await the train
branches.cn: 等火车

definition_zh: 机械的；与机器或力学有关的；不加思考的、机械式的
definition_en: relating to machines or to mechanics; also done by habit without thought
core_image: 一组齿轮咬合着转动，其中一枚缺了齿，仍在原处空转，发出规律的咔嗒声
scene: 打开机壳后，一排齿轮仍在咬合转动，其中一枚缺了齿，却还在原处空转。 The lift stopped because a mechanical fault jammed the door, not because of the power cut.
sceneCN: 这里 mechanical 指与机器部件有关的（第 2 个义项：机器部件方面的）；句意：电梯停下是因为机械故障卡住了门，而不是因为停电；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 机械的；力学的；机械式的
机械部件（罕用，复数形式指机械结构）

senses.title: Relating to machines
senses.definition: concerning machines or their parts rather than human or electronic action
senses.definitionCN: 涉及机器或其部件，而非人或电子动作
senses.example: A mechanical clock needs winding once a day.
senses.exampleCN: 机械钟每天要上一次发条。
senses.why: the adjective was built on the Greek word for a device, so its first job is to mark things of that kind.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词建在希腊语「装置」一词上，因此首要作用是标记同类事物。

senses.title: Of a machine's working parts
senses.definition: describing a fault or action that belongs to moving parts, not to power or software
senses.definitionCN: 描述属于运动部件的故障或动作，而非电力或软件
senses.example: The mechanic found a mechanical cause for the noise.
senses.exampleCN: 技工找到了噪声的机械原因。
senses.why: when a system has layers, the adjective isolates the layer of gears, bearings and seals.
senses.whyCN: 当系统分层时，这个形容词专门标出齿轮、轴承与密封件那一层。

senses.title: Belonging to mechanics as a science
senses.definition: concerning the study of forces and motion rather than chemistry or electricity
senses.definitionCN: 涉及力与运动的研究，而非化学或电学
senses.example: The paper sits on the boundary between mechanical and electrical effects.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇论文处在力学效应与电学效应的交界上。
senses.why: the same Greek root names a branch of physics, and the adjective follows it into the classroom.
senses.whyCN: 同一个希腊词根也命名物理学的一个分支，形容词便随之进入课堂。

senses.title: Automatic, without thought
senses.definition: done by habit or rule with no attention behind it
senses.definitionCN: 凭习惯或规则完成，背后没有留意
senses.example: His apology sounded mechanical and convinced no one.
senses.exampleCN: 他的道歉听起来很机械，谁也没被说服。
senses.why: a machine repeats without judging, and human behaviour that repeats without judging borrows the word.
senses.whyCN: 机器重复而不判断，人不判断地重复行为时便借用这个词。

senses.title: Barely varying, routine
senses.titleCN: 几乎不变的、例行公事的
senses.definition: describing a process that repeats identically with no adjustment
senses.definitionCN: 描述一模一样重复、毫无调整的过程
senses.example: The grading was mechanical: same comments, different names.
senses.exampleCN: 那次评分很机械：评语都一样，只是名字不同。
senses.why: repetition without variation is the visible signature of a machine at work.
senses.whyCN: 毫无变化的重复，是机器运转时最显眼的特征。

senses.title: Describing a physical breakdown
senses.definition: used of a failure caused by wear, jam or breakage of parts
senses.definitionCN: 用于因磨损、卡死或断裂造成的失效
senses.example: Mechanical damage is cheaper to prevent than to repair.
senses.exampleCN: 机械损伤预防起来比修理便宜。
senses.why: engineers divide failures by cause, and this adjective labels the cause that lives in the hardware.
senses.whyCN: 工程师按原因给故障分类，这个形容词标记住在硬件里的那一类。

senses.title: Of mechanical advantage
senses.definition: concerning the ratio by which a tool multiplies force
senses.definitionCN: 涉及工具放大力量的比值
senses.example: A lever gives mechanical gain at the cost of distance.
senses.exampleCN: 杠杆以距离为代价换取机械上的增益。
senses.why: the science of mechanics measures how tools multiply force, and that measure carries the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 力学测量工具如何放大力量，这一测量便带着这个形容词。

senses.title: Of reproduction by machine
senses.definition: describing copies made by a device rather than by hand
senses.definitionCN: 描述由装置而非手工做出的复制
senses.example: Mechanical copies of the print are worth far less than the original.
senses.exampleCN: 那幅版画的机械复制品比原作便宜得多。
senses.why: the age of printed multiples made the word a standard label for copies a machine produces.
senses.whyCN: 印刷复制品的时代让这个词成了机器所产副本的标准标签。

senses.title: Of a device's touch and feel
senses.definition: describing switches or keys that act through physical parts
senses.definitionCN: 描述通过实体部件动作的开关或按键
senses.example: She still prefers a mechanical switch for typing.
senses.exampleCN: 打字时她仍偏爱机械开关。
senses.why: users distinguish a real moving part from a touch surface, and the old adjective draws the line.
senses.whyCN: 用户要区分真正的运动部件与触摸表面，旧形容词正好划出这条线。

senses.title: Drawn with instruments
senses.definition: describing technical drawing done with rulers and compasses rather than freehand
senses.definitionCN: 描述用直尺与圆规而非徒手完成的技术制图
senses.example: The old course began with mechanical drawing before design.
senses.exampleCN: 那门旧课程先教机械制图，再教设计。
senses.why: before printing, precision came from instruments, and drawing by instrument took the adjective's name.
senses.whyCN: 在印刷之前，精确来自仪器，用仪器绘图便取了这个形容词的名字。

intro.en: Mechanical comes from Greek mekhane, a device or means, through Latin mechanicus. The adjective first meant belonging to machines and later came to mean unthinking.
intro.cn: mechanical 来自希腊语 mekhane「装置、手段」，经拉丁语 mechanicus 而来。形容词最初指「属于机器的」，后来引申为「不加思考的」。

items.en: Greek mekhane meant a machine, a device or a means of doing something, and mekhos meant a means or expedient.
items.cn: 希腊语 mekhane 指机器、装置或做事的手段，mekhos 指手段或办法。

items.en: The adjective mekhanikos described what belongs to devices or to inventive skill.
items.cn: 形容词 mekhanikos 描述属于装置或属于巧思技艺的事物。

items.en: Latin mechanicus kept the Greek sense and was used of mechanical arts and of engineers.
items.cn: 拉丁语 mechanicus 保留希腊含义，用于机械技艺与工程人员。

items.en: English mechanical first meant of machines and of the science of mechanics, with no hint of dullness.
items.cn: 英语 mechanical 最初指机器与力学，还没有「呆板」的暗示。

items.en: Newtonian mechanics made the adjective the standard label for force and motion, and the noun mechanics followed.
items.cn: 牛顿力学让这个形容词成为力与运动的标准标签，名词 mechanics 随后出现。

items.en: Industry and bureaucracy made repetition visible, and the adjective acquired its modern meaning of acting without thought.
items.cn: 工业与官僚制度让重复变得显眼，这个形容词于是获得「不假思索」的现代含义。

note.en: The first group is the same machine root in other shapes; the second group is the neighbouring words for automatic and machine-made.
note.cn: 第一组是同一「机器」词根的其他形式；第二组是「自动」与「机器制造」的相邻说法。

entries.definition: One who repairs machines; the adjective describes what belongs to machines.
entries.definitionCN: 指修理机器的人；形容词描述属于机器的事物。

entries.definition: The study of forces and motion; the adjective's third sense points to it.
entries.definitionCN: 研究力与运动的学问；形容词的第三个义项指向它。

entries.definition: The assembly of parts that produces an action; the adjective describes such parts.
entries.definitionCN: 指产生某个动作的部件组合；形容词描述这类部件。

entries.definition: In a machine-like or unthinking way; it tells how something is done.
entries.definitionCN: 以机器般或不假思索的方式；它说明做事的方式。

entries.definition: Working by itself once set going; mechanical stresses the parts, automatic stresses the lack of a hand.
entries.definitionCN: 一旦启动便自行工作；mechanical 强调部件，automatic 强调不需人手。

entries.definition: Done with the hands; it is the direct opposite of mechanical action.
entries.definitionCN: 用手完成的；是机械动作的直接对立面。

entries.definition: Regular and unvarying; routine describes the pattern, mechanical describes the absence of thought.
entries.definitionCN: 规律而少变化；routine 描述模式，mechanical 描述缺少思考。

entries.definition: Stiff and emotionless in manner; a modern synonym for the figurative sense of mechanical.
entries.definitionCN: 举止僵硬而无感情；是 mechanical 比喻义的现代同义说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations from the real Greek root and the real technical phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：来自真实希腊词根与真实技术搭配。

normal.en: Mekhane is a device, so mechanical means device-like before it means unthinking.
normal.cn: mekhane 是装置，所以 mechanical 先表示「像装置的」，再表示「不假思索的」。

normal.en: The family is regular: mechanic, mechanics, mechanism, mechanically.
normal.cn: 词族很整齐：mechanic、mechanics、mechanism、mechanically。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: mechanical failure, mechanical advantage, mechanical repetition.
normal.cn: 固定搭配分开义项：机械故障、机械效益、机械的重复。

normal.en: The adverb ends in -ly, and the comparison uses more and most.
normal.cn: 副词以 -ly 结尾，比较级用 more 与 most。

normal.en: It contrasts with manual, which is the hand against the gear.
normal.cn: 它与 manual 相对：一只手对着一个齿轮。

abstract.en: Picture a gear with one tooth missing, still turning because nothing has told it to stop.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚缺了齿的齿轮还在转，因为没人告诉它该停。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that apologises on a schedule, never looking up.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手按时间表道歉，从不抬头。

abstract.en: Picture a drawing so straight that the ruler is still visible in the ink.
abstract.cn: 想象一张画得极直的图，墨迹里还看得见尺子。

examples.en: Mechanical wear, not bad code, caused the shutdown.
examples.cn: 造成停机的是机械磨损，而不是糟糕的代码。

examples.en: His replies were polite but entirely mechanical.
examples.cn: 他的回答礼貌，却完全是机械式的。

examples.en: Mechanical drawings from that era still guide the repair shop.
examples.cn: 那个年代的机械制图至今仍指导着修理车间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米（me）卡（cha）你扣（ni-cal）」——米粒卡住你扣动的地方，正是机械出了毛病

root: 希腊 mekhane「装置、手段」→ mekhanikos「装置的」→ 拉丁 mechanicus → 英语 mechanical；力学义随牛顿力学固定，比喻义「不假思索」起于近代工业与官僚重复。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses move from machines to their working parts, the science of mechanics, unthinking habit, routine, breakdown, force ratios, machine copies, the feel of a switch and instrument drawing.
sensesIntro.cn: 十个义项从机器出发，经过工作部件、力学、不假思索、例行重复、损坏、力比、机器复制、开关手感，最后到仪器制图。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of meshing gears, one tooth missing, still turning and clicking in place.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排咬合的齿轮，其中一枚缺了齿，仍在原处转动并咔嗒作响。

branches.en: MACHINE AND PARTS: things of that kind, and specifically the moving layer inside a system.
branches.cn: 机器与部件：同类事物，以及系统中运动的那一层。

branches.en: SCIENCE OF FORCE: mechanics as a subject, and the measured gain a tool gives.
branches.cn: 力的科学：作为学科的力学，以及工具提供的可测增益。

branches.en: AUTOMATISM: acting without attention, and repeating without variation.
branches.cn: 自动性：不留神地行动，以及毫无变化地重复。

branches.en: HARDWARE IN THE WORLD: physical breakdown, and the feel of a real moving switch.
branches.cn: 现实中的硬件：实体损坏，以及真实运动开关的手感。

branches.en: MADE BY INSTRUMENT: copies produced by a machine, and drawings produced by a ruler.
branches.cn: 由器械造成：机器生产的复制品，以及用尺规画出的图纸。

intro.en: Mechanical is a Greek adjective ending on a Greek noun; English later added -ly for the adverb and -s for the science noun.
intro.cn: mechanical 是希腊名词加希腊形容词词尾；英语后来又加 -ly 成副词、加 -s 成学科名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin mechanicus is the borrowing that carried the Greek adjective into European languages; the ending -ical reached English through French forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mechanicus 是把希腊形容词带入欧洲语言的借词；词尾 -ical 经法语形式进入英语。

items.example: The noun is the source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是整个词族的源头。

items.example: The adjective supplies the ending that English kept.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词提供英语所保留的词尾。

items.example: The ending turns the adjective's field into a science.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把形容词所指领域变成一门学问。

items.example: The ending builds the word for an assembly of parts.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成「部件组合」的名称。

items.example: The adverb describes the manner of action.
Latin used the adjective as a name for a worker.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把这个形容词用作工人的名称。

items.example: The Latin word for hand is the base of the direct opposite.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语「手」是它的直接对立词的词基。

scene: 候机厅里他抬手看表。 The businessman checked his watch before the meeting.
