definition_en: for a limited time only, not permanently
core_image: 一把写着「借用」的钥匙，到期就要还
scene: 修桥期间，车辆改走临时便道。 Cars will temporarily use the side road while the bridge is closed.
sceneCN: 这里 temporarily 是「暂时地」（第 1 个义项：仅在有限时间内）；句意：桥封闭期间车辆将暂时改走便道。

derivatives.zh: 暂时的；临时的（副词的形容词形式，-ly 为副词后缀）
暂时性（形容词加 -ness 构成的抽象名词）

senses.title: For a limited time only
senses.definition: for a period that ends, not forever
senses.definitionCN: 只在会结束的一段时间内，而非永久
senses.example: The lift is temporarily out of service.
senses.exampleCN: 电梯暂时停用。
senses.why: The word simply points to an end date: whatever it touches carries a notice of expiry.
senses.whyCN: 这个词只是标出一个终点：凡被它形容的事物都自带「到期」提示。

senses.title: As a stopgap meanwhile
senses.definition: for the time being, until a permanent arrangement exists
senses.definitionCN: 在永久安排出现之前的当口
senses.example: They live temporarily with relatives while house-hunting.
senses.exampleCN: 找房子期间他们暂时住在亲戚家。
senses.why: Temporary time is not empty: it is a bridge walked while the real plan is built.
senses.whyCN: 临时的时间并非空白：它是真正方案落成之前所走的一段桥。

intro.en: Temporarily is the adverb of temporary, from Latin temporarius, of time, built on tempus, time.
intro.cn: temporarily 是 temporary 的副词形式，源自拉丁语 temporarius「属于时间的」，词基为 tempus「时间」。

items.en: Tempus meant time or season; its genitive temporis explains the r in the family.
items.cn: tempus 意为时间或时节；其属格 temporis 解释了词族中的 r。

items.en: Temporarius meant lasting only for a time, belonging to a season.
items.cn: temporarius 意为只延续一段时间的、属于某时节的。

items.en: Temporary entered English in the sixteenth century as a learned borrowing.
items.cn: temporary 于十六世纪作为书面借词进入英语。

items.en: The adverb temporarily formed with the native -ly ending.
items.cn: 副词 temporarily 用本族 -ly 后缀构成。

items.en: Modern life multiplied the word: temporary work, files, closures and visas.
items.cn: 现代生活令该词激增：临时工、临时文件、临时关闭与临时签证。

note.en: Temporarily is compared with its own family and with adverbs of short duration.
note.cn: 将 temporarily 与自身词族及表示短时长的副词对比。

entries.definition: the adjective meaning lasting a short time
of the same time; modern
speed, originally of music, from tempus
for a short time
until things change
for a moment, or very soon

normalIntro.en: Real links: tempus time, the temporary family, and signs that promise an end date.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：tempus 时间、temporary 词族，以及各种写明到期日的告示。

normal.en: Tempus means time; temporarily means inside a slice of it.
normal.cn: tempus 意为时间；temporarily 意为在一段时间之内。

normal.en: Temporarily closed: the door will open again.
normal.cn: temporarily closed：门终会再开。

normal.en: Contemporary shares the time root: living in the same slice.
normal.cn: contemporary 共享时间词根：活在同一段时间里。

normal.en: A temporary job is one with a built-in last day.
normal.cn: 临时工自带一个写好的最后一天。

normal.en: Temporarily unavailable means wait, not never.
normal.cn: temporarily unavailable 意为等等，而非永不。

abstract.en: An end date is a small mercy: nothing lasts forever, so nothing blocks forever.
abstract.cn: 终点日是一种小小的慈悲：没有什么是永久的，因此也没有什么会永远挡路。

abstract.en: The adverb is a hinge between two arrangements.
abstract.cn: 这个副词是两种安排之间的合页。

abstract.en: Time lends, never gives.
abstract.cn: 时间只出借，从不赠予。

examples.en: The server is temporarily down for maintenance.
examples.cn: 服务器因维护暂时停机。

examples.en: He temporarily put the keys on the window ledge.
examples.cn: 他暂时把钥匙放在窗台上。

examples.en: Prices rose temporarily after the storm.
examples.cn: 暴风雨后价格短暂上涨。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「贪婆瑞丽」——贪婆只是瑞丽一时，打扮是暂时的，卸了装就还原 → temporarily 暂时

root: 拉丁语 tempus（时间，属格 temporis）→ temporarius（只属于一段时间的）→ temporary → 加 -ly 构成副词 temporarily。

sensesIntro.en: One sense core: time with a visible exit, used for closures, loans and stopgaps.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项核心只有一个：带可见出口的时间，用于停用、借用与权宜安排。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clock with an alarm set for the end.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只已设好终点闹钟的钟。

branches.en: Anything labelled temporarily is promised to change back.
branches.cn: 凡标上 temporarily 之物都被承诺会变回原样。

branches.en: Signs and notices love this adverb.
branches.cn: 告示牌偏爱这个副词。

branches.en: The interim is walked, not lived in.
branches.cn: 过渡期只是被走过，而非定居。

branches.en: A bridge word: it connects before and after.
branches.cn: 一个桥梁词：连接前后两种状态。

branches.en: Every temporary stay carries a return ticket.
branches.cn: 每次暂住都揣着返程票。

intro.en: Temporarily sits in the tempus time family with temporary, contemporary and tempo.
intro.cn: temporarily 属 tempus「时间」词族，与 temporary、contemporary、tempo 同族。

latinIntro.en: Latin tempus, time, has genitive temporis; Latin temporarius meant of time, transient.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tempus「时间」，属格 temporis；temporarius 意为「属于时间的、短暂的」。

definition_zh: 树干；躯干；（汽车）后备箱；大象的长鼻；大箱子
definition_en: the thick main stem of a tree, a person's body without the head and limbs, the luggage space of a car, or an elephant's long nose
core_image: 一棵老树的粗壮主干笔直立在草地上，上面分出许多枝
scene: 森林边缘立着一棵很老的树，裸露的主干比旁边的人还粗。 The trunk of the old oak was wider than two men.
sceneCN: 这里 trunk 是「树干」（第 1 个义项：树木粗壮的主干）；句意为这棵老橡树的树干比两个人还宽。草地上那根粗壮笔直的树干，就是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: trunk 的复数，也指「（男式）泳裤」
由 trunk 加 -ful 构成，义为「一大箱之量」
由 trunk 加 -less 构成，义为「没有树干的」

senses.title: The main stem
senses.definition: the thick central stem of a tree, from which the branches grow
senses.definitionCN: 树木粗壮的主干，枝条从其上生出
senses.example: The trunk of the old oak was wider than two men.
senses.exampleCN: 这棵老橡树的树干比两个人还宽。
senses.why: Latin truncus meant the cut-off stem of a tree, and the branches were what had been trimmed away.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 truncus 指被截断的树干，被修去的正是枝条。

senses.title: The body without limbs
senses.definition: the main part of a human or animal body, without head, arms, or legs
senses.definitionCN: 人和动物除去头、四肢之外的主体部分
senses.example: He kept his trunk still and turned only his head.
senses.exampleCN: 他让躯干保持不动，只转过头。
senses.why: A body has a central column from which limbs branch, exactly as a tree has a stem and branches.
senses.whyCN: 身体有一根中央立柱，四肢像树枝一样从上面分出，与树干分枝完全一致。

senses.title: The car's storage space
senses.definition: the covered space at the back of a car for luggage
senses.definitionCN: 汽车后部放行李的带盖空间
senses.example: The bags were still in the trunk when we arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 我们到时行李还在后备箱里。
senses.why: Early travellers used a large chest, a trunk, and the car simply gave that chest a fixed home.
senses.whyCN: 早年旅人用一只大箱子，也就是 trunk，汽车只是给这只箱子安了固定的家。

senses.title: The elephant's long nose
senses.definition: the long flexible nose of an elephant
senses.definitionCN: 大象长而灵活可弯的鼻子
senses.example: The elephant lifted water with its trunk.
senses.exampleCN: 大象用鼻子吸水。
senses.why: The nose is a strong tube growing out of the face, so it borrows the word for a thick stem.
senses.whyCN: 这条鼻子是从脸上伸出的粗管，于是借用了粗壮主干的说法。

senses.title: The big travelling chest
senses.definition: a large box with a hinged lid, used for storing or carrying things
senses.definitionCN: 带翻盖的大型箱柜，用于存放或携带物品
senses.example: An old leather trunk stood at the foot of the bed.
senses.exampleCN: 床边放着一只旧皮箱。
senses.why: The word for a stem turned into the word for a box, because a trunk was once a hollowed log.
senses.whyCN: 树干一词变成了箱子的名称，因为早期的箱子就是一段掏空的木筒。

intro.en: Trunk comes from the Latin truncus, the stem of a tree with its branches cut off, and English extended it to bodies, boxes, and noses.
intro.cn: trunk 来自拉丁语 truncus，指被截去枝条的树干，英语把它扩展到躯干、箱子和象鼻。

items.en: Truncus meant maimed or cut short, as well as the stem left after pruning.
items.cn: truncus 意为被截断的，也指修剪后剩下的主干。

items.en: French tronc named the stem of a tree and the body of a person.
items.cn: 法语 tronc 指树干与人的躯干。

items.en: English trunk first named the body, then the hollow log used as a box.
items.cn: 英语 trunk 先指躯干，再指用作箱子的一段空木筒。

items.en: The word spread to the elephant's nose and later to a car's luggage space.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到象鼻，后来又指汽车的行李空间。

items.en: Trunks in the plural still name a short garment worn by swimmers.
items.cn: 复数形式 trunks 至今指游泳者穿的短裤。

note.en: The first group shares the trunk stem, the second holds other words for stems and bodies.
note.cn: 第一组共享 trunk 词干，第二组收其他表示主干与躯体的词。

entries.definition: Swimming shorts, or several chests.
As much as a trunk holds.
Having no trunk.
The long thin part of a plant above the root.
The human body without head and limbs.
A large strong box with a lid.

normalIntro.en: Trunk is one word with one idea carried far: a central thick body from which things branch or into which things are packed.
normalIntro.cn: trunk 一个词一条思路走得很远：中央的粗壮主体，枝条从它分出，东西往它里面装。

normal.en: A tree has a trunk on top, a car has one at the back.
normal.cn: 树的主干在上方，车的 trunk 在后方。

normal.en: Truncus in Latin meant cut short, the root of truncate.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 truncus 意为截短，是 truncate 的词根。

normal.en: The plural trunks can mean swimming shorts.
normal.cn: 复数 trunks 可以指泳裤。

normal.en: An elephant uses its trunk as a hand and a cup.
normal.cn: 大象把鼻子当手也当杯子用。

normal.en: Put the luggage in the trunk of the car.
normal.cn: 把行李放进汽车后备箱。

abstract.en: A bare column of bark rising out of the moss.
abstract.cn: 一根裸露的树皮柱从苔藓里立起。

abstract.en: A wooden chest with brass corners and a curved lid.
abstract.cn: 一只铜包角、弧盖的木箱。

abstract.en: A thick tube curling down to the water.
abstract.cn: 一根粗管弯下来伸向水面。

examples.en: Moss covered the trunk and the lower branches.
examples.cn: 青苔覆满了树干和下部的枝条。

examples.en: He swung the heavy case into the trunk of the car.
examples.cn: 他把沉重的箱子甩进汽车后备箱。

examples.en: The elephant curled its trunk around the small tree.
examples.cn: 大象用鼻子卷住那棵小树。

dict_mnemonic.text: trunk 从树的主干出发：人的躯干是主干，箱子是木筒，象鼻是粗管，后备箱是箱子。

root: 拉丁语 truncus（截短的、树干），经古法语 tronc 进入英语；同源词有 truncate、trunkful、trunkless。

sensesIntro.en: The tree stem opens the list, then the body, then the car space, the elephant nose, and the travelling chest.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是树干，再是躯干，然后是后备箱、象鼻与旅行大箱。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick column of bark on the moss.
core.cn: 核心意象：苔藓上一根粗树皮柱。

branches.en: The plant branch: the stem that holds the crown.
branches.cn: 植物分支：撑起树冠的主干。

branches.en: The body branch: limbs branch from a centre.
branches.cn: 躯体分支：四肢从中央分开。

branches.en: The container branch: the hollow log became a box.
branches.cn: 容器分支：空木筒成了箱子。

branches.en: The animal branch: a tube that can hold water.
branches.cn: 动物分支：能盛水的管子。

branches.en: The shape branch: thick, strong, and central.
branches.cn: 形状分支：粗壮而居中。

intro.en: Trunk is a Latin stem taken whole into English, and the family grows with -s and -less.
intro.cn: trunk 是整体借入英语的拉丁词干，词族靠 -s 与 -less 扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin truncus, cut short, also yields truncate and the words below.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 truncus（截短）还生出 truncate 以及下面的词。

items.example: The stem carries the idea of what is left after cutting.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干承载被截后剩下的部分。

items.example: The noun names the central body.
It forms trunks, several chests or shorts.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 trunks，多只箱子或泳裤。

items.example: It forms trunkful, one full chest.
It forms trunkless, without a stem.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 trunkless，没有树干的。

items.example: The verb keeps the literal old meaning.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词保留了字面的古义。

items.example: The ending shows the result of cutting.
It describes a tree with a strong stem.
items.exampleCN: 它形容有粗壮树干的树。

definition_zh: 私下地；不公开地；暗自；私立地；以私人身份
definition_en: in a way that is not open to the public or to other people; also used of institutions that are owned and funded by individuals rather than by the state
core_image: 一扇门关上，门后两个人压低声音说话
scene: 饭桌上人多，父亲没有提那件事，等客人走了才把儿子叫进书房，关上门。 She told me privately that the offer had already been refused.
sceneCN: 这里的 privately 是「私下地、不公开地」（第 1 个义项：不让外人知道地）；句意为她私下告诉我，那个提议已经被拒了。图中可辨识物件：关上的书房门、两只压低的肩膀。

pos.zh: 私下地；不公开地；暗自；私立地；以私人身份

derivatives.zh: privately 去掉副词后缀 -ly 得到的形容词，义为「私人的；私下的；私有的」
与 private 共用词干 priv-，加名词后缀 -acy 构成，义为「隐私；独处的状态」
由 private 加动词后缀 -ize 构成，义为「使私有化」

senses.title: In a way kept from the public
senses.definition: in a way that is not open to the public or shared with people outside a small group
senses.definitionCN: 不向公众开放、也不让小组以外的人知道地
senses.example: The deal was discussed privately before any announcement.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔交易在公布之前先私下讨论过。
senses.why: The Latin participle privatus described something set apart from public life, and the adverb simply carries that separation into the manner of an action.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语分词 privatus 指「从公共生活中被分出去的东西」，副词把这层隔开直接带进了做事的方式：做的时候把公众留在门外。

senses.title: In secret, so that others do not hear
senses.definition: in a quiet, concealed way, especially when other people are not supposed to know
senses.definitionCN: 安静而隐蔽地，尤指在不该让别人知道的情况下
senses.example: He privately hoped the plan would fail.
senses.exampleCN: 他暗自希望这个计划失败。
senses.why: Once the word means apart from others, it can also describe what happens inside a person's mind, where no audience can follow.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词的意思是「与旁人隔开」，它也能形容发生在一个人心里、没有观众跟进的事，于是从「背着人做」滑到「心里暗自」。

senses.title: Owned or run by an individual rather than the state
senses.definition: by a private owner, company, or charity rather than by the government
senses.definitionCN: 由私人、公司或慈善机构而不是由政府拥有或经营地
senses.example: The clinic is privately funded and charges no fee.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所由私人出资，不收取费用。
senses.why: Private began as a contrast with public office; applied to money and institutions, the same contrast turns into the difference between state control and individual ownership.
senses.whyCN: private 最早是与「公职」相对而言；把这个对立用到钱和机构上，就成了国家经营与私人所有之间的区别，副词则回答「由谁出钱、由谁办」。

senses.title: In one's personal capacity, not as an official
senses.titleCN: 以私人身份；以个人名义
senses.definition: as an individual rather than in an official or public role
senses.definitionCN: 以个人身份而不是官方或公共职务的身份
senses.example: She visited the camp privately, without cameras or guards.
senses.exampleCN: 她以私人身份探访营地，没有带摄像机，也没有警卫。
senses.why: The same line between the person and the office is redrawn here: the visit is real, but it happens outside the role that would make it public business.
senses.whyCN: 这里划的还是「人」与「职务」之间那条线：探访确实发生了，但发生在职务之外，所以不构成公共事务。

intro.en: Privately is the adverb of private, a word taken from Latin through French; its core is not secrecy but being set apart from the public.
intro.cn: privately 是 private 的副词形式，private 经法语借自拉丁语；它的核心不是「秘密」，而是「被隔离在公众之外」。

items.en: The verb privare meant to set apart, to strip away, or to deprive someone of something, and it supplies the stem behind the whole family.
items.cn: 动词 privare 意为分开、剥离、使失去，整族词的词干都来自它。

items.en: The participle privatus described a person or thing withdrawn from public office and belonging to an individual, which is the sense English still keeps.
items.cn: 分词 privatus 指从公职中退出、归个人所有的一个人或一件东西，这正是英语保留的那层意思。

items.en: Old French prive carried the Latin sense of personal and intimate, and also the newer colour of concealed or secret.
items.cn: 古法语 prive 承接拉丁语「个人的、亲近的」之义，又添上「隐蔽的、秘密的」这层新色彩。

items.en: Middle English used prive as an adjective and privily as its adverb, a form that survived in legal and literary writing long after the adjective changed shape.
items.cn: 中古英语用 prive 作形容词、privily 作副词；形容词后来改了形，privily 却在法律与文学文本里留了很久。

items.en: Modern English formed privately by adding -ly to private, and this regular form gradually replaced the older privily in everyday use.
items.cn: 现代英语在 private 后加 -ly 造出 privately，这个规则形式在日常使用中逐步取代了更古老的 privily。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin stem priv- and its English shapes; the near-meaning group gathers words for doing something out of public view.
note.cn: 形近组沿拉丁词干 priv- 及其英语词形展开；近义组收表示「不在公众视野里做」的词。

entries.definition: The adjective behind the adverb, meaning belonging to one person or kept from the public.
entries.definitionCN: 副词背后的形容词，义为「个人的」或「不公开的」。

entries.definition: The state of being alone or free from public attention.
entries.definitionCN: 独处或不受公众注意的状态。

entries.definition: Sharing in a secret; the word now survives mostly in legal phrases such as privy council.
entries.definitionCN: 参与秘密的；这个词如今主要留在 privy council 一类法律短语里。

entries.definition: An older adverb meaning secretly, largely replaced by privately in modern use.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「秘密地」的古老副词，现代英语中大多已被 privately 取代。

entries.definition: In a way intended to keep others from knowing.
entries.definitionCN: 以不让别人知道的方式。

entries.definition: In a way that treats what is said as something not to be passed on.
entries.definitionCN: 把所说的话当作不可外传的内容来处理地。

entries.definition: Inside one's own mind, without showing the feeling outside.
entries.definitionCN: 在内心深处，不把感受表露出来地。

entries.definition: With little noise or fuss, often so as not to attract attention.
entries.definitionCN: 声音小、不声张，常是为了不引起注意。

normalIntro.en: The word is Latin privatus with an English -ly, and every branch of the family turns on one idea: what is cut off from the public.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语 privatus 加英语后缀 -ly，整族词都绕着同一个意思转：从公众那里被切出去的部分。

normal.en: Privare in Latin means to set apart, so private is not mainly about secrets but about a boundary drawn around something.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 privare 意为分开，所以 private 主要不是讲秘密，而是讲在某个东西周围划了一道界。

normal.en: The same stem gives privacy, the state of being inside that boundary, and privation, the state of having been stripped of something.
normal.cn: 同一词干给出 privacy（待在这道界内的状态）与 privation（被剥掉东西的状态）。

normal.en: Privately is private plus -ly, the ordinary English way of turning an adjective into an adverb of manner.
normal.cn: privately 是 private 加 -ly，这是英语把形容词变成方式副词最普通的方式。

normal.en: In privately owned, the adverb answers a question about money: who paid, the state or an individual?
normal.cn: 在 privately owned 里，这个副词回答的是钱的问题：谁出的资，国家还是个人？

normal.en: The older adverb privily appears in old legal texts; both forms existed side by side before privately won.
normal.cn: 更古老的副词 privily 出现在旧法律文本里；两种形式并存过一段，最后 privately 胜出。

abstract.en: A word for being cut off from the public turns into a word for doing things behind a closed door, which is how privacy becomes a kind of action.
abstract.cn: 一个表示「与公众切开」的词，变成了「关起门来做」的词，隐私就这样从状态变成了动作。

abstract.en: Privately is a small grammatical hinge: it adds no new meaning to private, it only tells you the manner in which something is done.
abstract.cn: privately 是一个小小的语法铰链：它没给 private 添新意思，只告诉你事情是以什么方式做的。

abstract.en: The state can own a road and a family can own a house, and the same adverb quietly marks which of the two is speaking.
abstract.cn: 国家可以拥有公路，家庭可以拥有房子，同一个副词悄悄标出了说话的是哪一边。

examples.en: They met privately to settle the dispute before it reached court.
examples.cn: 他们在诉诸法庭之前先私下会面解决了争端。

examples.en: The museum is privately funded and charges no admission fee.
examples.cn: 这家博物馆由私人出资，不收门票。

examples.en: He privately doubted that the team could finish on time.
examples.cn: 他暗自怀疑这个团队能否按时完成。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「普莱维特利」——把「私下」读成一串快速的低语：privately。

root: 拉丁语 privare（分开、剥夺）→ 分词 privatus（从公职中分出、属个人的）→ 古法语 prive → 中古英语 prive／privily → 现代英语 private 加 -ly 成 privately。同族还有 privacy、privation、deprive。

sensesIntro.en: The core is separation from the public; the senses divide by what is being kept apart — information, other people, ownership, or an official role.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「与公众隔开」；义项按被隔开的东西分开：信息、旁人、产权，或一个官方身份。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door closing on two people speaking in low voices.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇门关上，门后两个人压低声音说话。

branches.en: a door shut before a difficult conversation
branches.cn: 一场难谈的话之前关上的门

branches.en: a hope kept behind the teeth
branches.cn: 含在牙关后面没说出口的希望

branches.en: a clinic whose nameplate lists no government office
branches.cn: 门口牌子上没有政府部门的诊所

branches.en: a visit made without cameras
branches.cn: 不带摄像机的探访

branches.en: the same wall between public money and private money
branches.cn: 公共的钱与私人的钱之间那同一道墙

intro.en: The word is built from a Latin verb of separation, its participle, a French adjective and two English endings; the eight pieces below follow that line.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语中表示分开的动词、它的分词、一个法语形容词和两个英语词尾搭成，下面八条就沿这条线走。

latinIntro.en: Latin privare and its participle privatus stand directly behind the English family, so the cognates here are well recorded rather than reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 privare 及其分词 privatus 直接位于这族英语词背后，所以这里的同族词有明确记录，不是重构形式。

items.meaning: set apart, belonging to one person
belonging to one person, not public
to take something away from someone

definition_zh: 寒意；风寒；使变冷；使寒心
definition_en: a cold feeling, a mild illness caused by cold, or to make something cold
core_image: 打开冰箱门时扑面而来的白气
scene: 夜里风从窗缝里钻进来。 A chill ran down his back when the door creaked open.
sceneCN: 这里 chill 指「寒意」（第 1 个义项：突然感到的一阵冷）；句意是门吱呀一开，一股寒意顺着他的背脊而下。

collocations.phrase: send a chill down one's spine

senses.title: A feeling of cold
senses.definition: a sudden cold feeling in the air or in the body
senses.definitionCN: 空气里或身体上突然感到的冷
senses.example: There was a chill in the room before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 天亮前屋里有一股寒意。
senses.why: The Old English word for cold named the sensation itself, and that sense remains the core.
senses.whyCN: 古英语中表示冷的词本指这种感觉本身，这一义项始终是核心。

senses.title: To make something cold
senses.definition: to make food or drink cold without freezing it
senses.definitionCN: 让食物或饮料变冷但不结冰
senses.example: Chill the soup for an hour before serving.
senses.exampleCN: 上桌前把汤冰一小时。
senses.why: The noun became a verb for causing the sensation in an object.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词，表示为物体制造这种感觉。

senses.title: To frighten or discourage
senses.definition: to make someone feel fear or a sudden loss of hope
senses.definitionCN: 让人感到恐惧或突然失去希望
senses.example: The empty streets chilled the visitors.
senses.exampleCN: 空荡的街道让来访者心里发凉。
senses.why: Fear is felt as cold running down the back, so the cold word moved into emotion.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧常被感觉为背上一阵冷，于是表示冷的词转入情绪。

intro.en: Chill is an old English word for cold that later took on fear and cooling.
intro.cn: chill 是表示寒冷的一个古英语词，后来兼指恐惧与冷却。

items.en: Kal- named cold and coldness.
items.cn: 日耳曼语词根 kal- 指冷与寒冷。

items.en: Ciele named a cold feeling or a cold illness.
items.cn: 古英语 ciele 指寒冷的感觉或受寒之病。

items.en: Chil kept the sense of a shivering cold.
items.cn: 中古英语 chil 保留「冷得发抖」的意思。

items.en: The noun became a verb meaning to make cold.
items.cn: 名词转为动词，意为使变冷。

items.en: Chill also means to frighten, and chill out means to relax.
items.cn: 如今 chill 也指使人恐惧，而 chill out 意为放松。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ch- and short i, while the meaning group names cold and fear.
note.cn: 形近组共享 ch- 与短元音 i，近义组列出寒冷与恐惧。

entries.definition: a young person
a small hot pepper
rather cold in a unpleasant way
a low temperature or the feeling of it
the quality of being cold
to become hard and solid with cold

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the cold root, the shiver image and the chill out idiom.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用「冷」词根、发抖的画面以及 chill out 习语。

normal.en: Chill and chilly share one root: chill is the feeling, chilly is the weather.
normal.cn: chill 与 chilly 同根：chill 是感觉，chilly 是天气。

normal.en: Catch a chill is the old phrase for catching a cold.
normal.cn: catch a chill 是「着凉」的旧说法。

normal.en: A chill down the spine mixes cold and fear in one image.
normal.cn: a chill down the spine 把寒冷与恐惧合在一幅画面里。

normal.en: To chill drinks is to cool them; to chill a person is to frighten them.
normal.cn: chill drinks 是让饮料变冷，chill a person 是让人心里发凉。

normal.en: Chill out means relax, a modern and very common use.
normal.cn: chill out 意为放松，是现代极其常见的用法。

abstract.en: Picture white mist rolling out of an open freezer.
abstract.cn: 想象白气从打开冰柜里滚出来。

abstract.en: Picture a hand rubbing its arms in a cold corridor.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在寒冷的走廊里搓着胳膊。

abstract.en: Picture a hair rising on the back of a neck.
abstract.cn: 想象后颈上汗毛竖起。

examples.en: A chill came through the open window.
examples.cn: 一阵寒意从敞开的窗子透进来。

examples.en: They chilled the wine before dinner.
examples.cn: 他们在晚餐前把酒冰了一下。

examples.en: The ghost story chilled the whole room.
examples.cn: 那个鬼故事让整个房间的人都发冷。

dict_mnemonic.text: chill 与 chilly 同根：身上一阵冷是 chill，外面冷冷的天气是 chilly。

root: 源自古英语 ciele（寒冷、受寒），属日耳曼语词根 kal-（冷），后引申出「使冷却」与「使恐惧」。

sensesIntro.en: The cold sensation is the base, causing cold in an object gives the verb, and cold inside the body gives fear.
sensesIntro.cn: 寒冷的感觉是基础，让物体变冷给出动词义，而体内的冷给出恐惧义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sudden cold that makes the skin tighten.
core.cn: 核心意象：一阵让皮肤收紧的骤冷。

branches.en: The noun names air or body cold.
branches.cn: 名词义项指空气或身体上的冷。

branches.en: The verb cools drinks and food.
branches.cn: 动词义项让饮料与食物变凉。

branches.en: The fear sense chills a person.
branches.cn: 恐惧义项让人心里发冷。

branches.en: Both deal with temperature only.
branches.cn: 两者只涉及温度。

branches.en: Cold becomes a picture for fright.
branches.cn: 冷成了恐惧的画面。

intro.en: Chill expands into an adjective and two participles with little change of stem.
intro.cn: chill 扩展出形容词与两个分词，词干几乎不变。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic; the cold root kal- also lies behind cool.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干属日耳曼语，表示冷的词根 kal- 也藏在 cool 之后。

items.example: The wind was chilling his hands.
Chilled water was on the table.
The chiller keeps the milk fresh.
items.exampleCN: 冷却机让牛奶保持新鲜。

latinEntries.example: Ciele is the oldest form of chill.
latinEntries.exampleCN: ciele 是 chill 最古老的形式。

definition_en: slightly wet, usually in a cold and unpleasant way
core_image: 晾了一夜没收的毛巾，摸上去又凉又潮
scene: 雨停之后，墙角的砖摸上去又凉又潮。 The walls felt damp after the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 damp 指「潮湿的」（第 1 个义项：微微发潮发冷）；句意是雨后墙壁摸上去发潮。

senses.title: Slightly wet and cold
senses.definition: holding just enough water to feel cold and unpleasantly wet
senses.definitionCN: 含着一点水，摸起来又冷又不舒服
senses.example: The towel was still damp when I picked it up.
senses.exampleCN: 我拿起毛巾时，它还是潮的。
senses.why: The wetness is small, but the cold makes it impossible to ignore.
senses.whyCN: 水并不多，可那股凉意让人无法忽略。

senses.title: Moisture in air or wall
senses.definition: water held in the air or inside a solid material
senses.definitionCN: 藏在空气里或墙体内部的水分
senses.example: Damp had crept up the wall behind the cupboard.
senses.exampleCN: 潮气顺着柜子后面的墙往上爬。
senses.why: When water has no shape of its own, we name it as a presence.
senses.whyCN: 水没有自己的形状时，我们就把它当作一种存在来称呼。

senses.title: To make less strong
senses.definition: to reduce the strength of a flame, a sound, or a feeling
senses.definitionCN: 降低火势、声音或情绪的力量
senses.example: They damped the flames with wet cloths.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用湿布压住了火苗。
senses.why: Covering a fire with something wet is the oldest way to slow it.
senses.whyCN: 用湿的东西盖住火，是最古老的灭火办法。

intro.en: Damp came into English from Low German, where it first meant vapour rather than the wetness vapour leaves behind.
intro.cn: damp 来自低地德语，最初指水汽，而不是水汽留下的潮湿。

items.en: Damp named the vapour that rises from wet ground.
items.cn: damp 指湿地上冒起的水汽。

items.en: The word entered English for a mist that wets whatever it touches.
items.cn: 这个词进入英语，指碰到什么就把什么弄湿的雾气。

items.en: Damp shifted from the mist itself to the slight wetness left behind.
items.cn: damp 从雾气本身转指雾气留下的那点潮湿。

items.en: Damp down appeared, meaning to cover a fire so it burns slowly.
items.cn: 出现了 damp down，指盖住火让它慢慢烧。

items.en: Damp now mostly describes cold, unwelcome wetness in cloth or walls.
items.cn: 如今 damp 多形容布或墙上那种阴冷、不受欢迎的潮。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by a single letter, and the meaning group moves from mild wetness to soaked.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个字母，近义组则从轻微潮湿一路走到湿透。

entries.definition: a wall built across a river to hold water back
entries.definitionCN: 横在河上拦水的一道坝

entries.definition: to make something slightly wet
to condemn someone or something
slightly wet in a soft, often pleasant way
entries.definitionCN: 微微湿润，常带柔和、舒服的意味

entries.definition: having a lot of water vapour in the air
covered or soaked with water

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a towel that never dried and end with a fire being covered.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一条没晾干的毛巾开始，落到一堆被盖住的火。

normal.en: A towel left in the bathroom keeps the cold of the water that soaked it.
normal.cn: 忘在浴室里的毛巾，留着浸过它的那股凉。

normal.en: A damp wall writes its history in dark patches.
normal.cn: 潮湿的墙用深色的斑块写自己的历史。

normal.en: Damp air makes a coat feel heavier than it is.
normal.cn: 潮湿的空气让外套摸起来比实际更沉。

normal.en: Cover a fire with wet cloth and the flame goes quiet.
normal.cn: 用湿布盖住火，火苗就安静下来。

normal.en: If the cold comes with the water, damp is the word you want.
normal.cn: 如果凉意跟着水一起来，你要的词就是 damp。

abstract.en: Picture a cold hand pressed to a stone wall in autumn.
abstract.cn: 想象秋天里一只冰凉的手按在石墙上。

abstract.en: Picture steam rising where the sun hits wet ground.
abstract.cn: 想象太阳照在湿地上，水汽升起来。

abstract.en: Picture a wet cloth dropped over a small flame.
abstract.cn: 想象一块湿布盖在一小簇火上。

examples.en: The walls felt damp after the rain.
examples.cn: 雨后墙壁摸上去发潮。

examples.en: She wiped the table with a damp cloth.
examples.cn: 她用一块湿布擦了桌子。

examples.en: They damped down the fire before leaving the camp.
examples.cn: 离开营地前他们把火压小了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 damp 记成「潮」：字母 d 像一滴水，amp 像插头，插头受了潮就会发闷。

root: 源自古低地德语 damp（水汽），十四世纪进入英语，先指湿地上冒的雾气，十六世纪转为指雾气留下的那点湿冷；十八世纪起又有「压住火」的用法，潮湿与压灭其实是同一个动作的两面。

sensesIntro.en: From a cold wet surface, to the moisture hidden in a wall, to a fire covered until it dies.
sensesIntro.cn: 从湿冷的表面，到墙里藏着的潮气，再到被盖住而渐熄的火。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cold, slightly wet surface touched by the hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：手掌触到一片阴凉微湿的表面。

branches.en: A towel or wall that holds a little cold water is the first picture.
branches.cn: 含着一点冷水、摸起来发凉的毛巾或墙，是第一幅画面。

branches.en: The same water, when it hides in air or plaster, becomes a presence.
branches.cn: 同样的水藏进空气或墙灰里，就成了一种存在。

branches.en: Wetness laid over a flame takes its strength away.
branches.cn: 湿的东西盖到火上，就把火的力量拿走了。

branches.en: The wet surface and the hidden moisture are one water in two places.
branches.cn: 表面的湿和藏着的潮，是同一份水待在两个地方。

branches.en: Both senses are about water winning slowly, without force.
branches.cn: 两个义项都是水在慢慢地赢，不靠蛮力。

intro.en: Damp is a small family: the adjective, its verbs of wetting and slowing, and a set of compound labels.
intro.cn: damp 这一族不大：一个形容词、几个表示弄湿和减弱的动词，还有一批复合标签。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root here; the word came from Low German damp, meaning vapour.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，它来自低地德语的 damp（水汽）。

items.example: The dampness in the room never left.

items.meaning: a thing that reduces sound or spirit
items.example: Rain put a damper on the picnic.
The coat hung damply by the door.
They laid a damp-proof sheet under the floor.
items.exampleCN: 他们在地板下铺了防潮层。

items.meaning: to cover a fire or calm a feeling
items.example: He damped down his anger and spoke calmly.
items.exampleCN: 他压下怒气，平静地说话。

items.meaning: a layer that stops water rising in a wall
items.example: The old house has no damp course.
items.exampleCN: 这栋老房子没有防潮层。

definition_en: the quality of being made of different kinds of things or people
core_image: 一个盒子里装着形状颜色各不相同的物件
scene: 这个班级在年龄和背景上差异很大。 The class showed great heterogeneity in age and background.
sceneCN: 这里 heterogeneity 是「异质性」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这个班级在年龄和背景上差异很大。

derivatives.zh: 异质的；由不同成分组成的

senses.title: Being mixed
senses.definition: the state of being made of different parts
senses.definitionCN: 由不同部分构成的状态
senses.example: The class showed great heterogeneity in age and background.
senses.exampleCN: 这个班级在年龄和背景上差异很大。
senses.why: This is the scientific core sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是该词在科学语境中的核心义。

senses.title: Variety
senses.definition: a wide range of different kinds within a group
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体内部种类的广泛差异
senses.example: The heterogeneity of the city is its strength.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市的多样性正是它的力量。
senses.why: The same idea is used for human variety.
senses.whyCN: 同一概念也用于描述人的多样性。

intro.en: Heterogeneity is built from Greek roots meaning other and kind.
intro.cn: heterogeneity 由希腊词根构成，意为「别的」和「种类」。

items.en: Heteros meant other or different.
items.cn: heteros 意为别的、不同的。

items.en: Genos meant kind or family.
items.cn: genos 意为种类或族类。

items.en: Heterogeneus described mixed kinds.
items.cn: heterogeneus 形容混杂的种类。

items.en: Heterogeneity named the state of being mixed.
items.cn: heterogeneity 指混杂的状态。

items.en: Science gave it a precise statistical use.
items.cn: 科学赋予它精确的统计用法。

note.en: Heterogeneity is compared with look-alike words and with words for variety.
note.cn: 把 heterogeneity 与形近词以及表示多样性的词作比较。

entries.definition: made of the same kind
not following accepted beliefs
attracted to the opposite sex
a range of different things
many different kinds
a combination of different things

normalIntro.en: Heterogeneity is a box full of different kinds, not one kind repeated.
normalIntro.cn: heterogeneity 是装满不同种类的盒子，而不是同一种类重复。

normal.en: The class showed great heterogeneity in age and background.
normal.cn: 这个班级在年龄和背景上差异很大。

normal.en: The heterogeneity of the city is its strength.
normal.cn: 这座城市的多样性正是它的力量。

normal.en: Researchers measured the genetic heterogeneity of the group.
normal.cn: 研究者测量了该群体的遗传异质性。

normal.en: Cultural heterogeneity makes the team richer.
normal.cn: 文化上的差异让团队更丰富。

normal.en: Too much heterogeneity can make rules hard to apply.
normal.cn: 差异过大，规则就难以统一执行。

abstract.en: Heterogeneity is what a single word cannot hold.
abstract.cn: 异质性，是一个词装不下的东西。

abstract.en: A forest survives by its heterogeneity.
abstract.cn: 森林靠它的多样性存活。

abstract.en: Uniformity is quiet, but heterogeneity is alive.
abstract.cn: 齐整是安静的，多样才是活的。

examples.en: The class showed great heterogeneity in age and background.
examples.cn: 这个班级在年龄和背景上差异很大。

examples.en: The heterogeneity of the city is its strength.
examples.cn: 这座城市的多样性正是它的力量。

examples.en: Researchers measured the genetic heterogeneity of the group.
examples.cn: 研究者测量了该群体的遗传异质性。

dict_mnemonic.text: heterogeneity 是「异质性、多样性」，由 hetero-（别的）加表示种类的词根构成；cultural heterogeneity 是文化异质性，genetic heterogeneity 是遗传异质性。

root: 由希腊语 heteros（别的、不同的）与 genos（种类）组合，经中世纪拉丁语进入学术英语；字面是「由不同种类组成」，因此表示异质性、多样性。

sensesIntro.en: Heterogeneity is the state of being made of different kinds, or the variety that results.
sensesIntro.cn: heterogeneity 是由不同种类构成的状态，或由此产生的多样性。

core.en: One container, many kinds.
core.cn: 一个容器，许多种类。

branches.en: The class showed great heterogeneity in age and background.
branches.cn: 这个班级在年龄和背景上差异很大。

branches.en: The heterogeneity of the city is its strength.
branches.cn: 这座城市的多样性正是它的力量。

branches.en: A mixed state and its variety are two views of one fact.
branches.cn: 混杂的状态与由此产生的多样，是同一事实的两面。

branches.en: Researchers measured the genetic heterogeneity of the group.
branches.cn: 研究者测量了该群体的遗传异质性。

branches.en: Cultural heterogeneity makes the team richer.
branches.cn: 文化上的差异让团队更丰富。

intro.en: Heterogeneity is built from hetero-, a kind root, and the noun ending -ity.
intro.cn: heterogeneity 由 hetero-、表示种类的词根和名词后缀 -ity 构成。

latinIntro.en: The parts are Greek, joined in medieval Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 这些构件来自希腊语，在中世纪拉丁语中组合。

items.exampleCN: 这项研究测量了异质性。
文化差异塑造着这座城市。
遗传异质性使治疗更复杂。

definition_zh: 环；圈；扣环；循环；回路；环路；绕行
definition_en: a shape in which a line or rope curves back and crosses or nearly crosses itself, a ring used for fastening, a repeated cycle in a process or program, or the act of moving around something in a curve
core_image: 一段绳子被绕成圆圈，两头几乎相接，像刚打好的一个结
scene: 雨后的山路上，车灯照着前方一个弯回来的岔口。 The road loops around the hill before joining the highway.
sceneCN: 这里 loop 是「绕行、环行」（第 5 个义项：沿弧线绕过某物）；句意为这条路绕过山丘之后才接上公路。图中可辨识物件：山路、车灯、弯回来的岔口。

pos.zh: 环；圈；扣环；循环；回路；环路

derivatives.zh: 由 loop 加 -y 构成，义为「古怪的；脑子绕不清的」
由 loop 加 -ing 构成，义为「成环；循环往复」
由 loop 与 back 复合，义为「回环；环回路径」

senses.title: A curve that closes on itself
senses.definition: a shape made when a rope, wire or line curves round and crosses or nearly crosses itself
senses.definitionCN: 绳子、金属丝或线条弯回来、彼此交叉或几乎交叉时形成的形状
senses.example: She made a loop with the rope and hung it on the hook.
senses.exampleCN: 她用绳子打了个环，挂在钩子上。
senses.why: A line bent back on itself leaves the eye with a closed figure; the shape, not the material, is what the word first names.
senses.whyCN: 一条线弯回自身，在眼里留下一个闭合的图形；这个词最先命名的不是材料，而是这个形状。

senses.title: A ring used for fastening
senses.definition: a small ring or curved strip fixed to something so that a belt, hook or cord can pass through it
senses.definitionCN: 固定在物体上的小环或弧形条，用来让腰带、钩子或绳索引穿过去
senses.example: The belt goes through a leather loop at the waist.
senses.exampleCN: 腰带从腰间的一个皮环里穿过去。
senses.why: Once a rope's closed curve can hold another thing, the same outline can be sewn or moulded onto an object; the ring stays because it still does the holding.
senses.whyCN: 一根绳子的闭合曲线一旦能套住别的东西，同样的轮廓就可以缝上或铸在物件上；环之所以留下，是因为它仍在承担「套住」这件事。

senses.title: A repeated cycle in a process or program
senses.definition: a set of instructions or events that returns to its starting point and repeats, especially in computing
senses.definitionCN: 一组回到起点并不断重复的指令或事件，尤用于计算机领域
senses.example: The program got stuck in a loop and printed the same line forever.
senses.exampleCN: 程序卡在循环里，一直打印同一行。
senses.why: A closed curve has no exit; when the steps of a process follow one another back to the start, the path of that process looks like the curve, so the repeat borrows the name.
senses.whyCN: 闭合的曲线没有出口；当一个过程的步骤依次回到起点，这个过程走过的路径就像那条曲线，于是重复也借用了这个名字。

senses.title: To form a curve or ring
senses.definition: to make something into a curve that closes on itself, or to be shaped in that way
senses.definitionCN: 把某物弄成闭合的曲线，或本身以那种形状存在
senses.example: Loop the cable twice around the frame before tightening it.
senses.exampleCN: 把缆线在架子上绕两圈再拉紧。
senses.why: The noun names the closed shape; the verb turns that shape into an action and asks what the hands are doing to the material.
senses.whyCN: 名词命名的是闭合的形状；动词把这个形状变成动作，问的是双手正在对材料做什么。

senses.title: To move around something in a curve
senses.definition: to travel in a curve that goes round something and often comes back towards the starting side
senses.definitionCN: 沿着一条绕过某物、常常又回到出发一侧的曲线行进
senses.example: The path loops around the pond and returns to the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 这条小路绕过池塘，又回到门口。
senses.why: A traveller going round a hill traces the same closed line on the ground, so the name of the shape becomes a verb for the route.
senses.whyCN: 绕山而行的人在土地上画出的正是同一条闭合线，于是形状的名字变成了路线上的动词。

intro.en: Loop is first recorded in Middle English for a bend in a rope; where the word came from is still debated, and the modern technical senses grew out of that rope ring.
intro.cn: loop 最早见于中古英语，指绳子上的一处弯折；它的来源至今仍有争论，现代的技术义项都是从那个绳环生长出来的。

items.en: The earliest recorded loop names a bend or fold in a rope or cord, not yet a perfect circle.
items.cn: 最早记录的 loop 指绳子或细索上的一个弯折，还不一定是完整的圆。

items.en: One common suggestion links it to Old Norse hlaup, a leap, through the running knot that a pulled rope forms; another points to Middle Dutch loopen, to run. Neither is certain.
items.cn: 一种常见说法认为它与古诺斯语 hlaup（跳跃）有关，因为拉紧的活结会形成环；另一种说法指向中古荷兰语 loopen（奔跑）。两说都不确定。

items.en: By the sixteenth century loop covered any ring-shaped curve, including loops of ribbon, metal and lace.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，loop 已泛指任何环状曲线，包括丝带、金属和花边形成的圈。

items.en: Railways and telegraphy gave loop a closed route or circuit, as in a loop line that turns back on itself.
items.cn: 铁路与电报事业给 loop 添上「闭合路线、回路」的义项，如折返回原处的环线。

items.en: Computing made the repeated instruction cycle a loop, and sound and video added the sense of playing a passage over and over.
items.cn: 计算机把反复执行的指令周期叫作 loop，声音与影像又添上「反复播放一段内容」的义项。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms and compounds built on loop; the near-meaning group gathers words for rings, coils and repeated cycles.
note.cn: 形近组收由 loop 构成的变形与复合词；近义组收表示环、盘绕与循环的词。

entries.definition: Silly or slightly crazy, as if one's thoughts have gone round in circles.
entries.definitionCN: 由 loop 加 -y 构成，义为「古怪的；脑子像绕成圈一样糊涂的」。

entries.definition: The act of forming a loop, or a repeated replay of a passage.
entries.definitionCN: 由 loop 加 -ing 构成，义为「成环；循环播放」。

entries.definition: A small opening in a wall, and later a gap in rules that lets someone avoid them.
entries.definitionCN: 由 loop 与 hole 复合，原指墙上的窄孔，后指规则中的「漏洞」。

entries.definition: A path or signal that returns to its own source.
entries.definitionCN: 由 loop 与 back 复合，义为「回环；环回路径」。

entries.definition: A round shape or circular object, especially one with an open centre.
entries.definitionCN: 环；圆圈；强调圆形本身，不一定有交叉或回环。

entries.definition: A length of wire or rope wound into a series of circles.
entries.definitionCN: 盘绕的一圈；强调材料被螺旋状连续卷起。

entries.definition: A set of events that repeats in the same order.
entries.definitionCN: 循环；周期；强调事件按同样顺序重复，不强调形状。

entries.definition: A closed route that starts and ends at the same place, or a path for electric current.
entries.definitionCN: 闭合路线；电路；强调起点与终点相接的一整圈。

normalIntro.en: The word is anchored in a rope bent back into a ring, and its family keeps returning to circles, repeats and routes that come back.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词锚定在一根弯回成环的绳子上，它的同族词反复回到圆圈、重复以及折返回来的路线。

normal.en: Two o letters in the middle of loop look like two joined rings, which is exactly the shape the word names.
normal.cn: loop 中间的两个字母 o 像两个相连的圆圈，正好是这个单词所指的形状。

normal.en: In the loop means inside a circle of people who know something; out of the loop means left outside that circle.
normal.cn: in the loop 指在知道内情的圈子里；out of the loop 指被留在圈子外面。

normal.en: A computer loop repeats the same instructions until a condition stops it, because a closed path keeps returning to where it began.
normal.cn: 计算机的 loop 会反复执行同样的指令直到条件终止，因为闭合的路径总是回到起点。

normal.en: Loop back is what a road or a signal does when it turns round and comes back towards its source.
normal.cn: loop back 就是道路或信号折返、朝源头回来时所做的动作。

normal.en: Loopy adds -y to loop: thoughts that go round and round without reaching a clear end sound slightly mad.
normal.cn: loopy 在 loop 后加 -y：想法一圈圈绕却到不了清楚的终点，听起来就有点古怪。

abstract.en: A loop has no obvious exit; walking it once only brings you back to the same gate.
abstract.cn: 一个环没有明显的出口；走一圈只会把你带回同一扇门。

abstract.en: A circle of information works the same way: those inside hear everything, those outside hear nothing.
abstract.cn: 信息的圈子也是一样：圈内的人什么都听得到，圈外的人什么都听不到。

abstract.en: Habits are loops too, which is why breaking one means cutting the path rather than walking it faster.
abstract.cn: 习惯也是环，所以改掉一个习惯要切断路径，而不是走得更快。

examples.en: The road loops around the hill before joining the highway.
examples.cn: 这条路绕过山丘之后才接上公路。

examples.en: The program got stuck in a loop and printed the same line forever.
examples.cn: 程序卡在循环里，一直打印同一行。

examples.en: She made a loop with the rope and hung it on the hook.
examples.cn: 她用绳子打了个环，挂在钩子上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卢普」——绳子一绕就圈成个环；loop 就是环、圈，也指循环。

root: 中古英语 loop 最早指绳子上的弯折；词源一般认为与古诺斯语 hlaup（跳跃）或中古荷兰语 loopen（奔跑）有关，但两说都无定论；现代又引申出循环、环线、回路等义。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a line that bends back into a ring; the senses divide into the shape, the fastening ring, the repeated cycle, the act of forming a loop, and the act of travelling round.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一条弯回成环的线；义项由此分出形状本身、起固定作用的环、反复的循环、把东西弄成环的动作，以及绕行一圈的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope bent into a circle, its two ends almost meeting like a knot.
core.cn: 核心意象：一段绳子弯成圆圈，两头几乎相接，像一个刚打好的结。

branches.en: a rope curled into a ring on the floor
branches.cn: 地上盘成一圈的一段绳子

branches.en: a leather ring sewn onto a belt
branches.cn: 缝在腰带上的一个皮环

branches.en: a program printing the same line again and again
branches.cn: 程序一遍遍打印同一行

branches.en: hands bending a cable into a circle
branches.cn: 双手把缆线弯成一个圈

branches.en: a path going round a pond and back to the gate
branches.cn: 小路绕池塘一圈回到门口

intro.en: Loop is a single stem, but its compounds and suffixes show how a rope ring grew into computing and media.
intro.cn: loop 本身是一个不可再拆的词干，但它的复合词与后缀显示了绳环如何长进计算机与影音领域。

latinIntro.en: Loop has no recorded Latin source; its origin is uncertain and is usually discussed through Germanic words, so no Latin family is listed.
latinIntro.cn: loop 没有可靠的拉丁语来源；它的来源不确定，通常放在日耳曼语词里讨论，因此不列拉丁同族词。

definition_en: to ask for information, especially in a polite or official way
core_image: 推开办公室的门，礼貌地问一句「请问这里能报名吗」
scene: 她打电话到酒店，询问周末还有没有空房。 She called the hotel to enquire about a room for the weekend.
sceneCN: 这里 enquire 是「询问；打听」（第 1 个义项：为获取信息而提问）；句意：她打电话到酒店，询问周末是否有房间。

senses.title: To ask for information
senses.definition: to ask someone for information about something
senses.definitionCN: 向某人询问某事物的信息
senses.example: I called to enquire about the train times.
senses.exampleCN: 我打电话询问火车时刻。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to seek into, so enquiring is looking into a matter by asking.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「探入寻求」，所以 enquire 就是通过提问去了解一件事。

senses.title: To ask about someone's health
senses.definition: to ask how someone is, especially after illness or absence
senses.definitionCN: 询问某人近况，尤指病后或久未见面时
senses.example: She enquired after his mother at the end of the call.
senses.exampleCN: 通话结束时她问起了他母亲的身体。
senses.why: Asking for information naturally includes asking about a person's wellbeing.
senses.whyCN: 寻求信息自然包括询问一个人的状况。

senses.title: To investigate officially
senses.definition: to try to find out the facts about an event, especially officially
senses.definitionCN: 试图查明某事件的事实，尤指正式调查
senses.example: The committee will enquire into the causes of the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会将调查事故原因。
senses.why: Seeking information can become a formal process, which gives the investigative sense.
senses.whyCN: 寻求信息可以发展为正式程序，于是产生「调查」义项。

intro.en: Enquire comes from Latin inquirere, to seek into, from in- and quaerere, to seek; the en- spelling comes through French.
intro.cn: enquire 来自拉丁语 inquirere（探入寻求），由 in- 与 quaerere（寻求）构成；en- 拼写经法语而来。

items.en: Quaerere means to seek, ask, or inquire.
items.cn: quaerere 意为寻求、询问或探问。

items.en: Inquirere adds in- and means to search into or investigate.
items.cn: inquirere 加上 in-，意为深入查找或调查。

items.en: Old French enquerre changes the prefix sound and carries the verb toward English.
items.cn: 古法语 enquerre 改变前缀读音，并把这个动词带向英语。

items.en: Middle English enqueren keeps both the asking and the investigating senses.
items.cn: 中古英语 enqueren 兼有询问与调查两种含义。

items.en: Enquire and inquire split as British and Latin-style spellings.
items.cn: enquire 与 inquire 分化为英式拼写和拉丁式拼写。

items.en: British English often prefers enquire for asking and inquire for formal investigation.
items.cn: 英式英语常用 enquire 表示一般询问，用 inquire 表示正式调查。

note.en: Enquire is the British spelling beside inquire, and its meaning sits with ask, question, and investigate.
note.cn: enquire 是与 inquire 并行的英式拼写，词义与 ask、question、investigate 相邻。

entries.definition: to ask for information, the Latin-style spelling
a question or investigation
a question or official investigation
to say something in order to get an answer
to ask someone about something
to ask a question about something uncertain
to examine facts to find the truth

normalIntro.en: Enquire and inquire differ only in the first vowel, and both contain quire, the seeking sound also heard in question.
normalIntro.cn: enquire 与 inquire 只差第一个元音，两者都含 quire 这个「寻求」的音，也见于 question。

normal.en: Think of question inside enquire: to enquire is to ask a question.
normal.cn: 在 enquire 里想到 question：询问就是提出问题。

normal.en: Enquire about is the pattern for asking for details.
normal.cn: enquire about 是询问细节的搭配。

normal.en: Enquire after is only for asking about a person's health.
normal.cn: enquire after 只用于问候某人的健康。

normal.en: Enquire into is the formal phrase for investigating.
normal.cn: enquire into 是表示调查的正式短语。

normal.en: British writing often uses en- for general asking and in- for official inquiries.
normal.cn: 英式写作常用 en- 表示一般询问，用 in- 表示正式调查。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised politely at an information desk.
abstract.cn: 想象在问询台前礼貌地举起一只手。

abstract.en: Imagine a phone call that begins with a careful question.
abstract.cn: 想象一通以谨慎提问开头的电话。

abstract.en: Think of a clerk opening a file to check the facts.
abstract.cn: 想象职员打开档案核对事实。

examples.en: She enquired about the price of the tickets.
examples.cn: 她询问了票价。

examples.en: He enquired after her father's health.
examples.cn: 他问起了她父亲的身体状况。

examples.en: The judge will enquire into the handling of the case.
examples.cn: 法官将调查此案的处理过程。

dict_mnemonic.text: en-（进入）+ quire（寻求）＝深入寻求答案，即询问；这是拆词联想，不是谐音。

root: 拉丁语 in-（进入）+ quaerere（寻求）→ inquirere（深入查问）→ 古法语 enquerre → 中古英语 enquire，英式拼写保留 en-。

sensesIntro.en: Asking for information is the core, asking after a person is its social form, and enquiring into a matter is its official form.
sensesIntro.cn: 获取信息是核心，问候某人是它的社交形式，而调查某事是它的正式形式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: stepping toward a source of information and asking.
core.cn: 核心意象：走向信息源，开口发问。

branches.en: Asking for information is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 询问信息，是基本义项。

branches.en: Asking after someone applies the same act to a person's health.
branches.cn: 问候某人，把同一动作用于对方的健康。

branches.en: Investigating is asking in an official and sustained way.
branches.cn: 调查是以正式而持续的方式发问。

branches.en: Information about things and about people uses one verb.
branches.cn: 询问事物与问候人都用同一个动词。

branches.en: A simple question can grow into a formal inquiry.
branches.cn: 一个简单问题可以发展为正式调查。

intro.en: Enquire is a French-shaped verb built on the Latin seeking root quaerere.
intro.cn: enquire 是法语形态的动词，建立在拉丁「寻求」词根 quaerere 上。

latinIntro.en: The Latin in- means into, and quaerere means to seek, so inquirere is to seek into a matter.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁前缀 in- 表示进入，quaerere 表示寻求，所以 inquirere 就是「深入查问」。

items.example: En- appears in enquire and enquiry.
items.exampleCN: en- 出现在 enquire 与 enquiry 中。

items.example: In- appears in the Latin source inquirere.
items.exampleCN: in- 出现在拉丁语来源 inquirere 中。

items.example: Quaerere is the root of enquire and question.
items.exampleCN: quaerere 是 enquire 与 question 的词根。

items.example: Inquirere is the Latin source of enquire.
items.exampleCN: inquirere 是 enquire 的拉丁来源。
enquerre 把 in- 变成 en-。

definition_en: a thick string, an electrical wire with a cover, or a cord-like part of the body
core_image: 一根细绳绕在手上，勒出浅浅的痕
scene: 包裹摊在桌上，他找出一根绳子把它系紧。 He tied the parcel with a thin cord.
sceneCN: 这里 cord 指「细绳」（第 1 个义项：较粗的绳子）；句意是他用一根细绳把包裹捆好。

senses.title: A thick string
senses.definition: a length of thick string made of twisted threads
senses.definitionCN: 由多股线捻成的较粗绳子
senses.example: She hung the curtain with a silk cord.
senses.exampleCN: 她用一根丝绳挂起窗帘。
senses.why: Twisting many weak threads makes one strong line.
senses.whyCN: 把许多细弱的线捻在一起，就成了一条结实的线。

senses.title: An electrical cable
senses.definition: a covered wire that carries electricity to a device
senses.definitionCN: 把电送到电器的包皮导线
senses.example: The lamp cord was too short.
senses.exampleCN: 台灯的电线太短了。
senses.why: Power also needs a path, and the path is named like a string.
senses.whyCN: 电也需要一条路，而这条路就用绳子的名字来叫。

senses.title: A cord-like body part
senses.definition: a long thin part of the body that looks like a cord
senses.definitionCN: 身体中细长如绳的部分
senses.example: The spinal cord carries signals from the brain.
senses.exampleCN: 脊髓把信号从大脑传出去。
senses.why: Inside the body, nerves also travel in long twisted bundles.
senses.whyCN: 身体内部，神经也是成束地长距离行走。

intro.en: Cord comes from Greek khorde, a string of gut, through Latin chorda and Old French corde.
intro.cn: cord 来自希腊语 khorde（肠弦），经拉丁语 chorda 与古法语 corde 进入英语。

items.en: Khorde meant a string made from animal gut.
items.cn: khorde 意为用动物肠子做的弦。

items.en: Chorda named a string for a musical instrument.
items.cn: chorda 指乐器的弦。

items.en: Old French corde widened the sense to any strong string.
items.cn: 古法语 corde 把词义扩大到任何结实的绳子。

items.en: English cord named rope used in daily work.
items.cn: 英语 cord 指日常劳作所用的绳。

items.en: Electricity gave the word the sense of a covered wire.
items.cn: 电的应用让这个词获得了包皮电线的含义。

items.en: The body sense survives in spinal cord and vocal cords.
items.cn: 身体义项保留在 spinal cord 与 vocal cords 中。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin string base cord-, and the meaning group names other things that tie or carry power.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语的弦词基 cord-，近义组列出其他用于捆扎或导电的东西。

entries.definition: several musical notes played together
an official agreement between sides
friendly and warm in manner
a very strong thick cord
a thin cord used for tying

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with twisted threads in a hand, then move to a lamp cable and to the spine.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从手里捻起的细线开始，再到台灯的电线，最后到脊柱。

normal.en: Cord and chord sound the same but live in different worlds: one ties, one sings.
normal.cn: cord 与 chord 读音相同却分居两界：一个捆东西，一个唱歌。

normal.en: Twist several threads and you get a cord; twist many cords and you get a rope.
normal.cn: 几股线捻起来是 cord，许多 cord 再捻起来就是 rope。

normal.en: A lamp cord is just a string that carries power.
normal.cn: 台灯的电线，不过是一根送电的绳子。

normal.en: The spinal cord is a cord inside the backbone.
normal.cn: 脊髓就是脊柱里的一根索带。

normal.en: The -less form, cordless, means free of that string.
normal.cn: 加 -less 的 cordless，就是摆脱了那根线。

abstract.en: Picture three threads twisted into one line.
abstract.cn: 想象三股线被捻成一条。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp cord curling across a wooden floor.
abstract.cn: 想象一根灯线弯曲着铺在木地板上。

abstract.en: Picture a long white cord running down a spine.
abstract.cn: 想象一条长长的白色索带沿脊柱而下。

examples.en: She cut a length of cord to tie the box.
examples.cn: 她剪了一截细绳来捆箱子。

examples.en: Unplug the cord before you move the lamp.
examples.cn: 搬动台灯之前先拔掉电线。

examples.en: Damage to the spinal cord can be serious.
examples.cn: 脊髓受损可能很严重。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cord 记成几股线拧成的一根：能捆东西的是绳，能送电的是线，长在身体里的是索。

root: 源自希腊语 khorde（肠弦），经拉丁语 chorda（琴弦）与古法语 corde 进入英语，由琴弦引申为细绳、电线与索状组织。

sensesIntro.en: From a twisted string, to a cable carrying power, and at last to a cord inside the body.
sensesIntro.cn: 从捻成的细绳，到输送电力的电线，最后到身体里的一根索带。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin cord wound around a hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根细绳绕在手上。

branches.en: Twisted threads make a line strong enough to tie.
branches.cn: 捻起的线做成一条足够结实的捆扎线。

branches.en: A covered line carries power to a machine.
branches.cn: 包皮的线把电送到机器上。

branches.en: A cord in the body carries signals instead of current.
branches.cn: 身体里的索带传的是信号，不是电流。

branches.en: Both are long flexible lines with a job.
branches.cn: 两者都是有任务的长而柔韧的线。

branches.en: Power and nerve both travel along a named path.
branches.cn: 电力与神经都沿着一条有名字的路径行走。

intro.en: Cord comes from Latin chorda, a string, and forms corded, cordless and cording in English.
intro.cn: cord 来自拉丁语 chorda（弦），在英语里构成 corded、cordless 与 cording。

latinIntro.en: The string base cord- also appears in chord, accord and cordial.
latinIntro.cn: 弦词基 cord- 也出现在 chord、accord 与 cordial 中。

definition_zh: 合法地；依照法律地；从法律角度；（因符合法定条件而）在法律上
definition_en: in a way that is allowed or required by law, or as judged from the point of view of the law
core_image: 市政厅窗口的印章落在纸角上，纸还是那张纸，盖章前后它能做的事却完全不同

sceneCN: 这里 legally 指「依照法律、不违法的」（第 1 个义项：以合法方式）；句意为只有在市政厅窗口盖章之后，店主才能合法地把招牌挂上门楣。图中可辨识物件：印章、表单、窗口柜台、木招牌。

pos.zh: 合法地；依法地；从法律角度；在法律上

derivatives.zh: 合法性；法律上的有效性

senses.title: In a way the law allows
senses.definition: in a manner that is permitted by the law and not forbidden by it
senses.definitionCN: 以法律允许、未被法律禁止的方式
senses.example: Only after the clerk stamped the form could the shop legally hang its sign above the doorway.
senses.exampleCN: 只有在市政厅窗口盖章之后，店主才能合法地把招牌挂上门楣。
senses.why: Legal is the adjective of lex 'law', and the adverb -ly says the action matches that standard: what is done legally falls inside the permitted line.
senses.whyCN: legal 是 lex「法律」的形容词，副词词尾表示动作符合这一标准：合法地做的事落在许可线之内。

senses.title: As the law requires
senses.definition: in the way that a statute or regulation demands, whether or not one agrees with it
senses.definitionCN: 按法令或规章所要求的方式，无论个人是否赞同
senses.example: The landlord must legally give ninety days' notice before raising the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 房东涨租之前必须依法提前九十天通知。
senses.why: The same adverb covers permission and obligation, because a statute both permits and compels; the direction of the duty is read from context.
senses.whyCN: 同一个副词既覆盖许可也覆盖义务，因为法令既授权也强制；义务的方向靠上下文判断。

senses.title: Judged from the law's point of view
senses.definition: when assessed by the rules of law rather than by morality, custom or common sense
senses.definitionCN: 以法律规则而非道德、习俗或常识来评估
senses.example: Legally the contract is sound, though everyone agrees it was unfair.
senses.exampleCN: 从法律上看这份合同没有问题，尽管大家都认为它并不公平。
senses.why: Adverbs of viewpoint mark the frame being used, so legally at the head of a clause means 'in the legal frame, whatever other frames say'.
senses.whyCN: 表示视角的副词标出所用的框架，因此位于句首的 legally 意为「在法律框架内，不论其他框架怎么说」。

senses.title: With binding legal effect
senses.definition: so as to create rights and duties that a court would enforce
senses.definitionCN: 以至于产生法院会执行的的权利与义务
senses.example: Once notarised, the promise was legally binding on both families.
senses.exampleCN: 一经公证，这项承诺对两家都具有法律约束力。
senses.why: A document becomes real in law when the required form is completed, and the adverb names that completed state rather than the intention behind it.
senses.whyCN: 文件在形式上完成法定手续后，才在法律上生效；副词命名的是完成状态，而非背后的意图。

senses.title: By lawful procedure
senses.definition: through procedures and means that the law permits, especially in obtaining evidence or taking action
senses.definitionCN: 通过法律允许的程序与手段，尤指取得证据或采取行动
senses.example: The evidence was legally obtained, so the court admitted it.
senses.exampleCN: 证据是合法取得的，因此法院予以采纳。
senses.why: Procedure is where legality is tested in practice: a right result reached by a forbidden route is not legally reached.
senses.whyCN: 程序是合法性的实际检验处：用被禁止的途径得到的正确结果，在法律上不算取得。

senses.title: Meeting a statutory definition
senses.titleCN: 符合法定定义地（按法定标准）
senses.definition: according to a threshold or definition written into a statute, as with age or disability
senses.definitionCN: 按照写进法令的界限或定义，如年龄或残疾认定
senses.example: He is legally blind, though he still reads with a magnifier.
senses.exampleCN: 他在法律上属于失明，尽管他仍用放大镜读书。
senses.why: Statutes define words for their own purposes, so legally can mean 'by the official definition' even when ordinary usage would say otherwise.
senses.whyCN: 法令会为自己的目的给词下定义，因此 legally 可以表示「按官方定义」，即使日常说法并非如此。

senses.title: Recognised in legal status
senses.titleCN: 在法律上获得承认的（身份、关系）
senses.definition: in the status that the law recognises, as with a marriage or a registered charity
senses.definitionCN: 以法律所承认的身份，如婚姻或注册慈善机构
senses.example: They were legally married in a registry office, with two witnesses.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在登记处依法结婚，只有两位见证人。
senses.why: Status is conferred by registration, and the adverb separates the legal fact from any ceremony or private understanding.
senses.whyCN: 身份由登记赋予，副词把法律事实与任何仪式或私下理解区分开来。

senses.title: Qualified through legal training
senses.definition: by reason of professional legal training or qualification
senses.definitionCN: 凭借法律专业训练或执业资格
senses.example: She is legally trained but now writes about court reform.
senses.exampleCN: 她受过法律专业训练，如今撰写有关法院改革的文章。
senses.why: The adverb attaches to training as well as to acts, because a qualification is itself something the law recognises.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词也能附着于训练，因为资格本身就是法律所承认的东西。

intro.en: Legally is legal plus the adverb ending -ly. Legal comes from Latin legalis 'of the law', from lex 'law'; the deeper origin of lex itself is disputed.
intro.cn: legally 由 legal 加副词词尾构成。legal 来自拉丁 legalis「法律的」，出自 lex「法律」；而 lex 本身的更深来源存在争议。

items.en: Lex, genitive legis, meant a statute or a binding rule. It named the enacted rule, not the abstract idea of justice, which Latin kept for ius.
items.cn: lex（属格 legis）意为法令或有约束力的规则。它命名的是被制定的规则，而不是抽象的正义观念，后者在拉丁语中由 ius 承担。

items.en: Source uncertain (root of lex): lex is often connected with legere 'to read, to gather', but that link is a hypothesis; others derive it from a root meaning 'to lay down'. No single origin is established.
items.cn: 来源不确定（lex 的词根）：常有人把 lex 与 legere「读、收集」联系起来，但那只是假说；也有人把它追溯到表示「放置、立下」的词根。尚无单一结论。

items.en: Legalis 'of the law, lawful' was formed on the stem of lex and passed through French into English as legal in the medieval period.
items.cn: legalis「法律的、合法的」由 lex 的词干构成，经法语在中世纪进入英语，成为 legal。

items.en: The English adverb ending -ly, from Old English -lice, turns the adjective into a word describing how an act is done or from what angle it is judged.
items.cn: 英语的副词词尾源自古英语相应的词尾形式，把形容词变成描述「如何做」或「从哪个角度判断」的词。

items.en: As law became a profession, legally extended to training and qualification, not only to acts permitted by statute.
items.cn: 随着法律成为一门职业，legally 从「法令允许的行为」扩展到训练与资格。

items.en: The first dates for the adverb are approximate: legal is attested from the medieval period, while legally settles into its modern senses in the early modern centuries.
items.cn: 这个副词的最早年代为约数：legal 在中世纪已有书证，legally 则在近代早期逐渐定型为今天的各义。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin law word and differs only in shade; the second group names other kinds of conformity to rule.
note.cn: 第一组共享那个拉丁「法律」词，差别只在分寸；第二组是对规则的其他种类的符合。

entries.definition: The adjective: permitted by law, or belonging to law as a field.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词：法律允许的，或属于法律领域的。

entries.definition: The quality of being lawful, or the question of whether something satisfies the law.
entries.definitionCN: 合乎法律的性质，或某事物是否满足法律要求的问题。

entries.definition: To change the law so that something previously forbidden becomes permitted.
entries.definitionCN: 修改法律，使原先被禁止的事变为允许。

entries.definition: Forbidden by law; the negative prefix reverses the permission without changing the root.
entries.definitionCN: 法律所禁止的；否定前缀把许可翻转为禁止，词根不变。

entries.definition: Concerned with making statutes, from lex plus latum 'carried'; it describes the making, not the obeying.
entries.definitionCN: 与制定法令有关，由 lex 加「携带」的过去分词构成；它描述制定，而非遵守。

entries.definition: In a way allowed by law, using the everyday noun law rather than the Latin one.
entries.definitionCN: 以法律允许的方式，用的是日常的 law 而非拉丁词。

entries.definition: In accordance with the constitution, which outranks an ordinary statute.
entries.definitionCN: 依宪法而行，效力高于普通法令。

entries.definition: By the terms of a particular statute, used mostly in official and legal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 按某部具体法令的条款，多用于官方与法律文书。

entries.definition: So as to have legal effect; a valid act may still be illegal if the wrong person performed it.
entries.definitionCN: 以至于具有法律效力；有效的行为若由无权者作出，仍可能违法。

entries.definition: By a just or rightful claim, which may or may not coincide with the statute book.
entries.definitionCN: 凭正当权利，可能与成文法令一致，也可能不一致。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin law word, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「法律」词、真实的同族词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Lex is Latin for law, and -ly turns the adjective into the manner: in the manner of the law.
normal.cn: lex 是拉丁语「法律」，副词词尾把形容词变成方式：以法律的方式。

normal.en: The family runs legal, legally, legality, legalise, legalisation and illegal.
normal.cn: 同族词有 legal、legally、legality、legalise、legalisation 与 illegal。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the binding sense: legally binding, legally required, legally entitled.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出约束力义：具有法律约束力、法律要求、依法有权。

normal.en: Latin kept ius for justice and lex for the statute, a split English later lost.
normal.cn: 拉丁语用 ius 表正义、用 lex 表法令，这一区分后来的英语丢掉了。

normal.en: A stamp on a form is the everyday picture of something becoming legally true.
normal.cn: 在表格上盖章，就是「某事在法律上成真」的日常画面。

abstract.en: Picture a door that opens only when a seal is pressed onto the paper beside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门，只有把印章压在旁边的纸上，门才会开。

abstract.en: Picture two identical letters, one inside the envelope and one still on the desk, differing only by a date stamp.
abstract.cn: 想象两封一模一样的信，一封进了信封，一封还在桌上，只差一个日期戳。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler laid on a table to decide which of two nearly equal lengths counts.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上放着一把尺，用来判定两个几乎一样长的东西哪个算数。

examples.en: The company acted legally by publishing the audit in full.
examples.cn: 该公司完整公布审计报告，行为合法。

examples.en: Legally, the land belongs to the trust, not to the family.
examples.cn: 从法律上看，这块地属于信托基金，而不属于这个家庭。

examples.en: Anyone legally resident for five years may apply for citizenship.
examples.cn: 任何合法居住满五年的人都可以申请入籍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「legal（合法的）+ ly（地）」——以合法的方式 → 合法地

root: 拉丁 lex（属格 legis）「法令、规则」（更深词根存疑）→ legalis「法律的」→ 法语 → 英语 legal；加副词词尾构成 legally。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one stamp: the stamp permits an act, compels a notice, fixes the frame of judgment, gives a document force, certifies a procedure, meets a statutory threshold, confers a status and finally recognises a qualification.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一枚印章：印章许可一个行为、强制一项通知、设定判断的框架、赋予文件效力、认证一道程序、达到法定界限、授予一种身份，最后承认一项资格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one seal pressed on paper, after which the same paper can do entirely different things.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚印章压在纸上，同一张纸从此能做完全不同的事。

branches.en: TWO DIRECTIONS OF THE SEAL: what the statute allows and what it demands are the same line read outward and inward.
branches.cn: 印章的两个方向：法令允许什么与要求什么，是同一条线向外读与向内读。

branches.en: THE FRAME: the adverb can step outside any particular rule and simply say which lens is being used.
branches.cn: 框架：副词可以退到任何具体规则之外，只说明正在使用哪一副镜头。

branches.en: FORCE AND ROUTE: a document with the seal, and evidence gathered the right way, are power plus the path that earned it.
branches.cn: 效力与路径：盖了章的文件与按规矩取得的证据，是力量加上挣得它的那条路径。

branches.en: DEFINITION AND STATUS: a threshold in a statute and a registration in a register both make a legal fact.
branches.cn: 定义与身份：法令里的界限与登记册上的一笔，都在制造一项法律事实。

branches.en: THE QUALIFIED PERSON: training itself becomes something the law recognises.
branches.cn: 有资格的人：训练本身也成为法律所承认的东西。

intro.en: Legally is a Latin law root, an adjective ending and an English adverb ending stacked in order.
intro.cn: legally 是把拉丁「法律」词根、形容词词尾与英语副词词尾依次叠加的结果。

latinIntro.en: Latin lex, genitive legis, gives legal, legality, legislate and legitimate; the English -ly ending marks manner or viewpoint.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 lex（属格 legis）衍生 legal、legality、legislate 与 legitimate；英语的副词词尾标记方式或视角。

items.example: The root names the enacted rule.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名被制定的规则。

items.example: It forms the adjective of law.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示法律的形容词。

items.example: The adjective holds both senses at once.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词同时承载两义。

items.example: It forms the noun of being lawful.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「合乎法律」这一性质的名词。

items.example: The abstract noun of the standard.
It forms the verb of change.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示改变的动词。

items.example: The verb names the change in the statute book.
items.exampleCN: 动词命名法令文本上的改变。

items.example: It turns the adjective into an adverb.
The adverb carries permission, obligation and viewpoint.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词兼具许可、义务与视角。

items.example: It negates the adjective in illegal.
items.exampleCN: 它在「非法的」中否定形容词。
